News.title: Fallon Sherrock defeats Luke Littler to land £501,000 prize in one-leg event
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fallon Sherrock won the second biggest prize in darts history as she claimed £501,000 by beating Luke Littler in a one-off leg.

The 32-year-old was crowned the champion of Netflix show ‘Beat Luke Littler’ when she took out 501 in 15 darts.

She was the 15th competitor out of 20 to take on the double world champion after he had won 14 straight legs.

While Littler made light work of some of the amateurs, which included an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando’s manager, he came up short against a top quality opponent.

Sherrock threw a 180 and checked out with him stranded on 124.

Victory, and over half a million pounds, throws Sherrock back into the limelight again, seven years after she made history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship on her way to the third round.

Her place in the show attracted some criticism given her stature in the game, but she was delighted to prove her worth.

“I’m over the moon, I can’t believe I have just won a leg of darts and won half a million,” she told the Press Association.

open image in gallery Littler took on an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando’s manager (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“This is definitely one of those top moments because it’s like an opportunity to kind of show off the women’s stars, and I feel like I’ve kind of taken the opportunity again.

“I’ve shown in the past women what can do as well and you know it’s definitely going to be put up there because it’s definitely the biggest prize money that I’ve won.

“I’ve just beaten the best in the world, and I can’t say that very often.

“When I hit the 180, I was like, ‘right, just relax and just go for the shot out because this is probably the only shot that you’re going to get’.

“And I took it.”

Littler was not at his best in a truncated format which saw him one leg every 10 minutes.

Irish student Pearse Mackie, who was the eighth contestant to face Littler, was the first to have a dart for victory, but he missed bullseye to claim what would have been a memorable win.

Mark Pooke, who played Phil Taylor in a professional match almost 20 years ago, also had darts to win in the ninth leg, but could not take out 138.

Despite, having his pride dented by losing, the 19-year-old is keen to go again.

open image in gallery Luke Littler beat 14 contestants in the one-leg event in Manchester (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Yeah, (she was) brilliant. That’s what one person had to do. Win the bull and go out in 15,” Littler said on stage.

“That’s exactly what Fallon did. I hit a 140 to leave 142.

“When she missed the first going tops, I was like, ‘give me a chance’. She didn’t and world class.

“I’ve enjoyed every bit of it. The advert, the photo shoots, everything. It’s been good and maybe Netflix we can do it again next year.”

News.title: Canada and EU announce new alliance in response to hostility from Trump
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The European Union and Canada announced a new alliance of “ever-closer association” designed to bring together like-minded countries to address common challenges.

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said on Friday he and his European counterparts would define the scale and scope of a "new form" of European Union membership over the coming months, and that Canada would become its first "associate member."

They will define by a 2027 summit what the association would entail exactly, Carney said.

In a post on X, Carney said that what he called an “Alliance for the Future” would not only be open to Canada and the EU, but to “other countries that share our views to address common challenges and strengthen our collective power.”

open image in gallery European Council president Antonio Costa, Canada's prime minister Mark Carney and European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen attend a Signature Ceremony at the Canada-EU Summit in Montreal ( Reuters )

Donald ‌Trump last ‌month threatened trade sanctions in ⁠response to von der Leyen's proposal to create ⁠a new status for the EU-Canada relationship.

The US president has adopted a more transactional approach to foreign ​policy and has repeatedly attacked multilateral institutions.

Carney called Canada “the most European of non-European countries” early in Trump’s trade war. This week, it was reported that discussions regarding trade between the US and Canada had seen only modest advancement.

On Thursday, European Commission president Ursula ⁠von der Leyen said the EU ​and ⁠Canada continue to ‌explore the North American nation becoming the union's first "associate member," a term so divisive among member ‌countries that it does ‌not appear in the final statement.

Carney said the alliance between EU and Canada, announced at a summit in Montreal on Friday, would focus on resilience in areas including AI, energy and critical minerals.

"We are working towards the deepest possible partnership, short of accession," he said, adding that this would result in "Canada ‌becoming the European Union’s first Associate Member."

open image in gallery Mark Carney was in the UK last month, where he and Andy Burnham - both Evertonians - watched their side together ( Getty )

The associate member term, which Germany and several other EU countries oppose, has no legal meaning.

In a joint statement released to mark the end ⁠of the summit, Canadian and EU leaders cited an “unwavering commitment to effective multilateralism, democracy and to the rules-based international order."

The statement said Canada and the 27-nation EU would work to resolve the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East and deepen security ties elsewhere, including in the Arctic.

It added talks had been ‌concluded on a ​digital trade agreement that would ‌complement the existing trade agreement between ​Canada and the EU.

Carney also said he had accepted the European Council president's invitation to attend meetings in Europe next June, where he said talks on the deeper relationship would be concluded.

"We are building the industries and infrastructure that underwrite our collective security," Carney said.

"This is only the beginning."

News.title: G20 photocall cancelled after Miliband refuses to be pictured with Russian foreign minister
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The group photocall at Friday’s G20 meeting was cancelled after foreign secretary Ed Miliband and his European counterparts refused to be photographed with Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio was forced to pull the plug on the photograph at the start of the meeting of the world’s largest economies in Atlanta, Georgia, after several European officials said they intended to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off the gatherings.

Rubio decided to scrap the picture because he thought the controversy would be a distraction, according to two US officials, who spoke to the Associated Press.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the US invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Donald Trump pushed ties with Kyiv to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance.

In his intervention at Friday’s meeting, Mr Miliband said: “Let me say this directly to the Russian foreign minister – we all know who the aggressor in this war is.

“Let’s talk about what happened at Dnipro railway yesterday. Only yesterday your drones attacked and killed 15 people.

“And there are countless examples like this of you killing innocent civilians throughout this war.

“We all know you are the aggressor. We all know you started this war four and a half years ago with the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

open image in gallery The G20 foreign ministers' meeting took place in Atlanta, Georgia ( Reuters )

“And Putin thought then he would win this war easily. But you are not winning this war.

“Thanks to the courage of the Ukrainian people and the solidarity of countries round this table, you are not winning.

“If you had the courage to tell the truth and to do what is right you would tell Putin that he is not winning this war and will not win.”

A UK Government source told the Press Association: “We were not going to take part in any official picture with the Russian foreign minister.”

They added: “The Foreign Secretary is here in Atlanta focused on the global challenges that are driving up costs for people at home.

“The UK has a longstanding policy not to have direct, bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion of Ukraine and we are not about to change that.”

Polish deputy prime minister Radosław Sikorski told reporters in Atlanta that “I am not the only one who does not want to be photographed with Lavrov.”

German foreign minister Johann Wadephul said “there is no normality with Russia” as he explained there would be no photograph taken.

But he added “we must exchange the controversies at the table here,” the German news agency dpa reported.

He also said that “we also must not send falsely optimistic signals.”

open image in gallery Atlanta police officers stand guard along a street as a sign directs attendees to the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta ( AFP/Getty )

Lavrov has traveled only infrequently to NATO member states since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and resulting severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow.

Rubio still opened the talks with an appeal for unity on the issues that threaten international security and trade.

“We are in a critical moment,” he told his colleagues. “We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises.”

He pointed to disruptions to global energy and food supplies, trade and freedom of navigation and said many are posing “severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”

Yet there was no sign that the G20 diplomats could come to consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face.

Among them are the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese machinations in the South China Sea. All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel as well as uncertainty about trade.

Diplomats who attended the opening session described it as cordial but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland's membership in the G20 - the Associated Press reported.

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

News.title: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot
News.content:
David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

News.title: Trump administration loses grip on bird flu, experts warn
News.content:
The Trump administration has been criticised for losing control of a bird flu outbreak that has spread among mink and cattle farms across the United States.

The H5N1 virus has infected around 1,000 people since it was first detected in the late 1990s, killing roughly half of them. While it currently does not spread among humans, scientists have long worried that it could trigger a pandemic, and that each human infection raises the risk of the virus mutating.

A new variant emerged in 2020 and has since spread to millions of birds and hundreds of animal species across the globe, leading to devastating losses in both wildlife and farmed livestock and poultry.

While some countries have introduced tough measures to curb its spread, including mandatory culls of infected animals, “flockdowns” (where birds are kept indoors) and vaccination of farm workers who handle at-risk livestock, experts say the US is allowing the virus to run rampant.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged unchecked on a Utah farm that raises thousands of mink for fur, news outlet ProPublica reported last week.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

Mink have very similar respiratory systems to humans, increasing the risk that a virus can spread between the animals and people, and undergo a process known as “reassortment”, when two or more viruses mix together to make a new, more dangerous strain.

News.title: Britain faces unprecedented squeeze on incomes, IFS says
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has ruled out making “crude cuts” to welfare after he failed to tackle the rising benefits bill in Wednesday’s Budget.

The Chancellor acknowledged last night that the current benefits system is “unsustainable” but said he will only look to make cuts “in a Labour way”.

Speaking to the BBC in the wake of Wednesday’s Budget, Mr Healey promised that “there will be a reduction in the benefits bill” before the next election.

However, he said this will not include “crude cuts” to payments.

He said: “We will do that in a Labour way, and we will do that because it is simply not good for Britain, or progressive, to have a bigger and bigger benefits bills.

“This system is unsustainable. I’ve been clear about that. The Prime Minister’s been clear about that. It’s what you do about it.”

He added: “We have to bring the benefits bill down. You don’t do that by crude cuts, especially when people are feeling the cost of living pressures.”

His comments on welfare come after Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused Labour of presiding over a Government that had left Britain “overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system”.

She said: “Next year, under Labour, the tax burden will be the highest in our country’s history and our benefits bill is going up by tens of billions of pounds because this Government has put welfare first.”

The latest figures from the Office for Budget Responsibility released on Wednesday revealed that benefits spending is expected to jump by almost 30pc to £431bn by 2032.

Almost half the total is pensions and disability benefits for pensioners, despite the planned abolition of the triple lock. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey launches tax raid on savers as welfare bill spirals | Chancellor to pull in £4.3bn from landlords and savers as Badenoch calls for ‘tough love’ on benefits

2) Gulf states face tax raid on UK property investments | John Healey’s changes risk driving investment away from Britain, industry experts warn

3) UK hands Rolls-Royce £1.25bn to fund new jet engines | British engineering giant confirms plans for £2.5bn to be invested during next decade

4) Petrol drivers face threat of stealth tax raid to boost EVs | Official review recommends forcing fuel suppliers to fund new renewable energy subsidies

5) JP Morgan lashes out at ‘unprincipled’ bank tax | Wall Street giant criticises John Healey’s Budget announcement on surcharge increase

What happened overnight

The Chancellor will have woken up to jittery markets after Google-owner Alphabet revealed higher spending on AI.

Alphabet dropped 10pc in after-hours trading, wiping nearly $400 billion off its market value. Microsoft, by contrast, beat forecasts with better-than-expected cash flows that lifted its shares by 3pc.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.7pc, while Japan’s Nikkei fluctuated between gains and losses and was last ⁠up 1pc.

Oil prices retreated as investors latched onto hopes that peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict could be back on the table.

European stocks were on track to edge higher at the open after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as widely expected on Wednesday. The European Central Bank announces its next interest rate decision on Thursday.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa to SUE Jamie Carragher over ‘shut the f*** up’ comments about Man Utd as 37-word statement released
Sports.content:
Next

ASTON Villa are taking legal action against TV pundit Jamie Carragher over his ‘unacceptable insults’.

Villa co-owner and chairman, Nassef Sawiris, announced the controversial move on social media.



A short statement on the club’s own account appeared late on Friday night.

Sawiris has taken exception to Carragher’s remarks about Villa fans after urging Manchester United to make a move for manager Unai Emery – and that the Spaniard would want the Old Trafford job if Michael Carrick is sacked.



Carragher, speaking on the Stick to Football programme, said Villa supporters should shut the **** up and that ‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United’.

Those comments have been met with anger behind the scenes at Villa Park.

And Sawiris confirmed the club would not stand for it.

He said: “Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans.

“Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football.”

Earlier this week, Carragher spoke about reigning Europa League-winning manager Emery and the United job – insisting the Villa boss would not turn down the chance to take charge.



He said: “I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year.

“That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

“But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League – take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

“Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.



“But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.

“So Real Madrid will take Manchester United’s best player, they did it with Cristiano Ronaldo.

“And there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they’ll take their players or manager, so shut the **** up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.”

Emery attended the Ballon D’Or awards this week and said: “I am so comfortable here.”



He has made the club his own over his four years in charge and has complete control over football affairs.

Emery is unlikely to have that level of influence if he were to move to United.

Last week, he made it clear that he aims to take Villa into the Champions League every season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the summer, he lost six of team who won the Europa League in May.



But he replaced them and has now rebuilt the squad – they will aim for a third successive league victory when they take on Fulham at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Israeli West Ham star Manor Solomon branded a ‘baby killer’ by pro-Palestine thugs over national service with the IDF
Sports.content:
Next

WEST Ham star Manor Solomon has been branded a “baby killer” by pro-Palestine activists for serving with the IDF.

Thugs urged the club to “kick out” the Israeli in a campaign backed by local councillors.



Masked, hooded activists recorded a video outside the Championship club’s London Stadium in the east of the capital threatening the winger.

In a disguised robotic voice, one says: “We do not agree with the signing of Manor Solomon. We’ll continue to raise our voices until he is out of the club.”



It comes after some Irons fans chanted “Manor Solomon’s on my mind/And he hates Palestine” at the August 16 match at Burnley.

He had joined the club — who later urged the fans to stop — only days before.



The recent abuse against him was bolstered by the Tower Hamlets Palestine Solidarity Network, created and run by councillor Faysal Ahmed.

Sharing an image from the video, it wrote: “Activists hammer home the message: Kick out baby killer Manor Solomon from West Ham United.”

At least seven other Tower Hamlets councillors are members of the group’s Facebook page.

Solomon, 27, was enlisted for mandatory military service in the IDF — the Israel Defense Forces — in December 2017.



It was seven years before the Gaza attacks launched after Hamas slaughtered at least 1,195 Israelis on October 7, 2023.

Alex Hearn, of Labour Against Antisemitism, said: “Solomon’s done nothing except be an Israeli footballer. Hounding a player out of his job because of where he comes from is not activism, it’s bigotry. No elected councillor should be anywhere near it.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s not always rosy’ – Michael Carrick reveals how talks with Wilcox and Berrada went amid horror Man Utd run
Sports.content:

IT HAS allegedly been a week of “hard truths” at Manchester United.

Six difficult days of airing out tensions, crunch talks at every level and frank exchanges in the name of the greater good.



But there is one truth that nobody inside Old Trafford can talk their way around.

Boss Michael Carrick needs a result. And he needs one now.



Because all the uncomfortable conversations and dressing-room finger-pointing will mean nothing at all if the Red Devils cannot break this shameful eight-game winless streak.

All will be revealed on the Stamford Bridge pitch.



United — 16th in the Prem table just two points off the bottom — head to Chelsea for the lunchtime fixture, desperate to offer their downbeat manager a lifeline and drag themselves away from the relegation zone.

For once, Carrick has offered a glimpse into the talks he has with the men who are on the verge of axing him in CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Clubman Carrick never airs dirty laundry, especially with regard to internal dialogue, but clearly felt compelled to stress that he has stuck up for himself before the trip to West London.

The under-fire coach said: “It’s not always rosy with nice conversations between anyone.

“Whether that’s me and the players, whether that is between me, Jason or Omar or the owners. It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward.”

But supporters have heard this all before. Countless times.

The promises of a “different response” from underperforming players who might finally start showing up for their battered and bruised dugout.

Bruno Fernandes used to go to war for Old Trafford’s struggling managers.

Now the United captain looks infected by the same disease.



Fernandes, 32, and Carrick were at loggerheads before the reigning Premier League player of the year questioned the tactics after the 4-1 Como capitulation last week.

They held the second “hard truth” chat of the week after Carrick left the midfielder on the bench for Sunday’s 3-0 home drubbing by Bournemouth.

The pair aired their views before a wider squad debrief between players and coaches triggered further frosty back-and-forths away from the Amazon documentary cameras.



Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who dialled in for Monday’s tense boardroom sit-down before deciding to give Carrick a stay of execution, will know if talk is futile when he sits in the Blues’ directors’ box today.

United have not won away since the final day of last season at Brighton, when everything seemed dreamy before Carrick signed a two-year deal.

The British billionaire is being tipped to swing his axe toward Wilcox and Co, should a third manager be sacked under Ineos’ 2½-year watch.

The blame game has surely kicked off between Ratcliffe and the majority-owning Glazer family, who sold off the sporting operations of the biggest football club in the world to a group whose other soccer teams — Nice and Lausanne — were falling apart.

Fans gave the board the hardest truth when the Stretford End cheered for Carrick before uncorking deafening boos at the players once the gaffer was out of sight down the tunnel.



They know the soap opera is beyond Carrick’s remit.

Just £163million with add-ons was spent on four players in the summer meaning that United were outspent by new boys Hull (£179.3m) and Ipswich (£210.6m).

And despite being £1.1BILLION in debt, Ratcliffe is still focused on building a shiny new ground.



But Old Trafford sang: “You can stick your new stadium up your arse” in the club’s last Prem outing.

The £4.5bn valuation the AWOL Glazers put on the club when seeking a buyer four years ago is looking more unrealistic than ever.

The Glazers, for their part, may want to see United’s new Wembley of the North built before selling — but that may not be completed until 2035.

The hardest truth of all.

Roy Keane bashed the players for downing tools under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021.



A decade ago Carrick, then vice-captain, warned it was “disrespectful” to accuse the players of not trying hard enough during Louis van Gaal’s eight-game winless run.

Now in the hotseat, Carrick matched that unwanted record on Sunday and nine matches without a victory would break the 38-YEAR mark.

Carrick had a rare clear week after Brighton knocked them out of the League Cup at the first time of asking last month.

Extended time on the training ground proved vital in the second half of last campaign’s successful one-match per week run.

Sports.title: ‘I sat with mum in tears after two biggest dreams were ripped away,’ reveals Middlesbrough & Scotland star Tommy Conway
Sports.content:

TOMMY CONWAY experienced the darkest fortnight of his career when two of his biggest footballing dreams were ripped away in a single afternoon.

The Middlesbrough star limped off during the play-off semi-final against Southampton, knowing his ankle was in a bad way.



Sitting in a consultant’s office alongside his mum, Conway received the devastating news that he required immediate surgery.

That operation killed any chance of featuring for Scotland at the World Cup, despite being promised a spot in Steve Clarke’s squad.



To make matters worse, as he came out of surgery, Boro learned they were heading for Wembley after Southampton were expelled for Spygate.

The 24-year-old watched in agony as Boro suffered play-off final heartbreak against Hull, unable to help his team-mates.



Conway said: “That was the toughest thing I’ve ever had to overcome in my career mentally.

“I knew I was missing the World Cup — but to then find out we were back in the final at Wembley and had to watched on helplessly was awful.

“Things happen in life and you have got to accept it, move on and bounce back.

“I’ve told myself there is another World Cup in four years and I’m going to do all I can to be there.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Conway spent four months trapped in a grueling cycle of physical rehabilitation and mental frustration.

He added: “As a footballer, the worst thing in the world is being injured.

“The worst day of the week is Saturday at three o’clock when the team is going out and you’re on the sideline watching.

“Going through four months of pain mentally and physically, the day you step foot back on the pitch makes everything worth it.

“One of the best moments in a Boro shirt was coming back and the reception I got as I came on against West Brom at the Riverside. It was special.”



Now fully fit, Conway is channeling every ounce of that summer pain into firing Boro into the Premier League.

Kim Hellberg’s men host Charlton this weekend sitting top of the Championship.

And Conway has formed an instant bond with Teesside’s working-class faithful since arriving from Bristol City.

He said: “I feel like ever since I have come here, I’ve really taken to the area.

“I can see myself within people in this area. They’re hard-working, working class, which is where I come from.



“I can really vibe off everyone up here and it reminds me of how I grew up almost.

“They’re so passionate supporting the team. The way they travel in their numbers home and away is special.

“All I want to do when I step foot on the pitch is to give back to them.”

Conway’s game has soared under Hellberg, who made the bold decision to shift the forward to the left wing.

The switch has given him the freedom to terrorise full-backs in one-on-one battles.



Conway said: “Until Kim came in, I would have always said I was a striker.

“It was almost like he saw something in me playing off the left. It was a natural transition.

“Ever since I’ve gone out there, I’ve grown in confidence.



“The freedom to get at players 1v1 and really back my ability, he is the first coach who has really given me that confidence.

“When I go onto a pitch now, I’m the most confident I’ve ever been.”

Conway also credits former Boro boss Michael Carrick for filling his tactical locker with tips picked up from Manchester United’s glory years.

He revealed: “Some of the things I learned off Michael I probably never would have learned anywhere else from him playing at such a high level.

“The little details that he used to give me I still live by every day.



“He always used to speak to me about how Wayne Rooney used to finish — little things like shooting through defenders’ legs.

“Passing on bits from players he played with was valuable information.”

His mentality was forged during loan spells in non-league with Yate Town and Bath City as a teenager.

Conway said: “When I first went to Yate, I was 17. You are a young lad going into a dressing room of 30-year-olds.

“You show what you’re about in training and they soon realise you’re a good player.



“I remember going to the gym at half 10 at night after training at Bath, just to do something extra.

“All the lads walked past thinking, ‘Wow, he’s 18 years old and he’s in the gym doing this.’

“I was up against big centre-halves, so I had to learn quickly. I wasn’t the strongest, so had to be smarter.”

During his early days at Bristol City, Conway shared a house with best mate Alex Scott, now starring for Bournemouth.



The pair spent weekends glued to the television, plotting their rise to the top of English football.

Conway said: “Alex is my best mate in football. We lived together and I saw his rise as much as he saw mine.

“Me and Al always used to watch football. Super Sunday would be on and we’d say we want to play in the Premier League one day.

“He’s there now and I’m working away trying to get myself there. Hopefully soon enough I’ll be there with him.”

Conway is convinced that achieving promotion with Boro would top anything he could ever accomplish in the game.



He added: “I think about getting there with this club every day.

“It would give everyone such a boost. I pride myself on it and I almost want to take responsibility and make sure it does happen.”

Sports.title: Fleetwood’s epic win over Arsenal was something football’s elite could never manufacture with a bloated fixture list
Sports.content:
Next

SOME people in football believe the answer to every problem is another competition, another tournament, another round of matches — and another opportunity to sell something.

Then Fleetwood Town come and remind us the best thing about the game can’t be manufactured, marketed or guaranteed. It’s the possibility the impossible might happen.



The League Two club beat Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties to reach the quarter- finals of the Carabao Cup.

Cod Army are 84 places below the Gunners in the football pyramid and their visitors arrived with huge resources, an expensive squad and expectation they would go through.



But they left with a defeat that will live in Fleetwood folklore.

For a small club, it’s not just another fixture done but a night fans will tell grandchildren about.



Players become heroes, photographs go on walls and the result takes on a life of its own.

That is the romance of football, and it remains one of the most valuable things the sport possesses.

But the shock did raise the question over how much football is too much football?

Mikel Arteta made nine changes but still had Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz starting up front and Martin Odegaard also came on. It was not a team of strangers dragged off the training ground.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But the changes were significant as Arsenal looked ahead to a top-flight trip to Liverpool tomorrow.

Managers do not rotate to confuse fans but because players need rest, injuries accumulate and the consequences of running a squad into the ground can be far more damaging than an early domestic cup exit.

Arteta had a decision to make. He could prioritise this competition or manage the demands of a season in which every available date seems to have acquired a commercial purpose.

He chose to rotate and they lost but it’s unfair to suggest the selection alone cost them the game.

Fleetwood defended magnificently, their keeper Jay Lynch made crucial saves and their players took their penalties with extraordinary composure.



They deserved their moment.

That does not make the wider question any less important.

The Premier League is a global phenomenon and the Champions League has expanded while Fifa has enlarged the Club World Cup and shape an international calendar that hit elite players hard.



Each development arrives with an attractive sales pitch: more football, opportunities and revenue — and a bigger audience.

There is nothing inherently wrong with ambition as football is a business and money generated at the top helps support jobs and the wider game.

But there is a difference between growing a sport and assuming that its capacity for growth is unlimited.

The calendar is not an empty spreadsheet waiting to be filled, it contains human beings who need to recover, clubs that need to prepare and fans with finite time and money.

When another competition is added, something else has to give.



It can be recovery time or the quality of a performance or just the chance for a young player to develop without unreasonable burden. And sometimes it is just the competition itself.

The irony is football’s administrators risk damaging the very product they are trying to sell. Supporters do not fall in love with fixture lists.

They fall in love with stories, rivalries, moments of brilliance and knowing their club, however small, can achieve the extraordinary.



The FA Cup and the League Cup have always offered that hope and their value lies partly in the imbalance between the clubs taking part.

A little club versus the giant isn’t a flaw to be corrected; it’s the point.

If elite clubs increasingly have to treat domestic cup ties as obstacles to be managed around, the consequences will eventually reach beyond their own dressing rooms.

Smaller clubs depend on these occasions for revenue, exposure and memories money alone cannot buy so they need the big clubs to take the competitions seriously.

So Fifa and the other governing bodies should listen to concerns about congestion. It’s not an argument against international football or a demand that the richest clubs should always get their own way.



It is a call for decisions to take proper account of those who play it, run it and pay to watch it.

Fleetwood did not try to make a point about governance, they just took their chance to make history.

Arsenal’s resources could not buy a place in the next round and their hosts earned it the hard way.

Football’s rulers would do well to remember that distinction. They can sell the game around the world, expand competitions and calculate commercial value to the last pound.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But they cannot manufacture the feeling when a club that was never supposed to win discovers it can.



That is football’s magic. The challenge is to make sure that — in the rush to sell more of it — we do not lose what makes it worth watching in the first place.

EVERYONE might want to face Manchester United at the moment, but their trip to Chelsea spells serious danger for Xabi Alonso.

The Blues boss has flown under the radar somewhat since his arrival at Stamford Bridge.



After a chaotic, entertaining start and some encouraging wins over Bournemouth and Everton – it has all fallen quite flat.

An embarrassment at home to London rivals Tottenham, the butt of the joke in the Premier League of late, was followed by a Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool.



Another failure against this toxic and terrible Manchester United would seriously put the heat on Alonso.

Most of us would expect United’s downward spiral to continue the way things have been going in recent weeks.

However, we’ve seen over their years of struggling that, once the spotlight is turned on them, these Manchester United players can pull a performance and a result out of the bag when it is least expected.

But no one would consider that when putting Alonso under the microscope.

And would it really be a massive surprise if United leave west London with smiles on their faces and three points? No, because Chelsea cannot keep a clean sheet.

They have just two this season, against Everton and Luton Town. Given their expenditure at the back it is very poor.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

There are plenty of little signals to encourage United. Pedro remains injured, Maxence Lacroix is too and there is still no Emiliano Martinez.

It looked like Chelsea had turned a corner after their win over Everton, but now there are problems piling up and in goal they look to have someone, in Mike Penders, who cannot catch a ball again.

Like I said, a lot to encourage United to make a fast start and put them under pressure.

When Alonso arrived there were goals galore and we were looking at the most exciting front three in the Premier League with Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

People were, foolishly, tipping them to give Arsenal a run for their money in the hunt for the title.



But they were absolutely shocking at the back, and while there were injuries some of that has to go on the manager.

Those injuries mean it is hard to see exactly what Alonso wants them to be as a team. When you consider that the benefit of not being in European means there is so much more time for him to work with those who are fit, that has to be a concern.

Given where they are in the Premier League table, fifth and two points better off than Brentford having played fewer games in all competitions than everyone above them, that is not a lot to have sacrificed European football for.



Alonso is yet to face any real pressure or sustained heat from the fans, but this weekend could be the turning point.

The Spaniard arrived being hailed as the man to bring serious standards and professionalism to a petulant squad packed with potential. But that has not quite settled in yet either.

Attempts were made to add experience and move on some unruly characters, but that ideal is still being undermined by some silly players.

Palmer lost his head against Tottenham and was sent off. Rogers was fortunate not to get a second booking at Everton and arguably also lucky not to join Palmer in being given his marching orders against Spurs.

We are seeing too many of the same old Chelsea problems and Alonso must find a solution, fast. Not that his selections or comments over the past week have gone down too well.



Playing Rogers through the middle against Spurs was daft, when have we ever seen him look good doing that or want to play in that position? You are taking away the best of a player you broke records to sign by doing that.

They would never stick Moises Caicedo up there, would they?

And to add to some growing pressure from the fanbase, after going out to Liverpool this week Alonso said the quiet bit out loud by suggesting it was alright because the Carabao Cup is not that important anyway.

A strange thing to say.

We are a long way from serious, Michael Carrick-style questions being posed to Alonso – but he will be more aware than anyone that the honeymoon is well and truly over.

England's Red Roses responded to shock back-to-back defeats in Canada with a crushing 55-12 WXV Global Series victory over the USA in New Jersey, returning to winning ways.

John Mitchell's side entered the contest off the back of losing two Tests in a row for the first time in a decade, and having lost their 41-Test, four-year unbeaten run in Toronto.

The USA scored two tries through loosehead prop Hope Rogers and replacement back Kate Zackary, but shipped three second-half tries in nine minutes with prop Mona Tupou in the sin-bin due to repeat scrum penalties.

Sports.title: Leicester top table after victory over Bristol
Sports.content:
Leicester Tigers' Freddie Steward scores a try against Bristol

Leicester moved to the top of the PREM table with a bonus-point 22-16 victory over Bristol at Ashton Gate in an error-ridden game.

Tigers took advantage of Bristol having two men in the sin-bin to score 10 points in their absence, which ultimately proved the difference.

Leicester's tries came from Freddie Steward, Adam Radwin, Ollie Hassell-Collins and Jamie Blamire, with Billy Searle adding one conversion.

Louis Rees-Zammit scored the Bears' only try, with James Williams adding three penalties and a conversion to secure a losing bonus point.

Bristol took a sixth-minute lead thanks to a solo effort from the Welsh flyer Rees-Zammit. The wing received possession 35 metres out from the try-line, but from an unpromising position, he skipped past two defenders to race in under the posts.

Leicester's response was swift with bursts from Finn Carduff and Cameron Henderson putting the defence on the back foot before a well-judged cross-field kick from Searle saw Steward collect to crash over.

Bristol Bears' Louis Rees-Zammit is tackled by Leicester Tigers' Adam Radwan

Minutes later, the visitors looked to have taken the lead when their skipper Ollie Chessum forced his way over, but TMO replays showed the ball had gone forward when Aaron Wainwright's penetrative run was brought to an end.

Bristol also came close when Rees-Zammit was presented with another opportunity but under pressure from the challenge of Tom Whiteley, he just failed to collect his own kick ahead as the line beckoned.

The hosts then suffered two blows in quick succession when centre Mathias Moroni and full-back Tom Jordan were both yellow carded for dangerous challenges.

Leicester capitalised when an alert Searle sent a long kick deep into the opposition 22 with Radwan showing exceptional speed to be first to the ball and touch down.

Radwan almost had another when he chased another kick ahead, but this time he failed to gather so the Tigers had to be content with a 12-7 interval lead.

Ninety seconds after the restart, Leicester extended their advantage when another cross-field kick found Hassell-Collins in acres of space to score his side's third.

Bristol were brought back to full strength before Williams reduced the arrears with a straightforward penalty.

Basic handling errors from Radwan and replacement Will Wand gave the Bears the chance to build an attacking platform, but they were too frenetic to benefit until Williams knocked over a second penalty.

The game hung in the balance but the away pack produced an unstoppable line-out drive for Blamire to secure the bonus point, with Searle missing his third conversion to keep the home side in the hunt.

A third penalty from Williams, seven minutes from time, set up a tense finish, but the Tigers held on for a deserved victory despite Searle hitting a post with a last-minute penalty.

Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.

Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers.

Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.

Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap, leaving him 11th.

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton complained about a power issue before retiring from FP2 at the Mexico City GP

Max Verstappen, another to have sat out first practice, was three tenths off the pace in fifth, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar slotting in behind him.

Verstappen was involved in a bizarre collision with his former team-mate Liam Lawson in the early stages of the session as the four-time world champion attempted to overtake the Racing Bulls driver.

Lawson defended and retained track position, only for the battle to continue on for several more corners before the pair made contact, leaving debris on the track that caused a red flag to be thrown so it could be cleared.

The pair will not only have to explain themselves to their teams, who are both part of the Red Bull family, but also the stewards as they were called to see them following the session.

Lawson was ninth, two places behind his team-mate Arvid Linbdlad with Alpine's Pierre Gasly splitting the Racing Bulls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP

Oscar Piastri endured another disappointing day as he could only manage 10th, finishing more than half a second down on his McLaren team-mate Norris.

Fernando Alonso produced an encouraging result for Aston Martin as he finished within eight tenths of Leclerc in 12th.

"Overall, our performance looks quite alright but we still need to work on some of our limiting factors. It was quite tricky on track today, as the surface was slippery, so we will work on that to find some improvements for tomorrow," said Leclerc.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz and Bernie Collins explain why Ferrari's upgrade meant they were the only team not using their reserve driver during P1 in Mexico City

Antonelli had a low-key day considering he's expected to become world champion on Sunday as he never threatened to challenge Leclerc's pace.

"There are definitely more things we can improve going into tomorrow and we have some work to do overnight," said Antonelli, who won last time out in Austin.

"Ferrari looked very quick, but we will focus on ourselves, see where we can find more performance and hopefully put ourselves in a good position for tomorrow."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton remains uncertain over the severity of the problem with his Ferrari after he was forced to retire from the second practice session at the Mexico City GP

Should Antonelli fail to score points on Sunday, he can still become world champion if Hamilton or Russell fail to win the race.

Hamilton was off the pace throughout Friday compared to team-mate Leclerc but said he was "feeling really good in the car" before his technical issue.

"I think we did a really good job in getting the setup in a better place and just really unfortunate. I think we are really competitive this weekend as a team.

"I don't think I need to make many changes to the setup. I will probably leave it pretty much the same because we were very quick.

"I already had a loss of power earlier in the lap and we were still quick. I will give it everything tomorrow and try to do the best with whatever I have."

Sports.title: Canelo and Mbilli make weight for world title fight in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli both made the weight for their WBC super-middleweight world title fight on Saturday in Riyadh.

Canelo was 167.6lb with Mbilli a fraction heavier at 167.8lb.

Alvarez is looking to win back one of the world titles he used to hold in his first fight since his stunning loss to Terence Crawford last year.

When Crawford retired it left the four major world championships vacant and Mbilli became the WBC titlist.

"I'm the challenger now, but in my mind I've always been the champion, ever since I was a little kid," Canelo said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights as Crawford stunned Alvarez to become undisputed super-middleweight champion. Canelo vs. Crawford is available to watch globally only on Netflix

He elected to go straight in with Mbilli, a high-calibre, tough, aggressive fighter, right off the back of that defeat.

"I don't believe in shortcuts. I want to become a world champion again, and that's why I want to face the best. Mbilli is the world champion," Canelo said.

Mbilli, unbeaten with only one draw in his 30-fight professional career, declared: "I have a lot of respect for Canelo and his career, and I congratulate him on everything he has achieved. But inside the ring, it will be a different story, and I'm coming to win.

"I'm ready to shock the world."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at occasions when boxers seemed to slow down time in a fight and make their opponent miss with everything

The event in Riyadh is going ahead amid escalating conflict in the region.

Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi airports, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, while security concerns have led to the postponement or cancellation of other sporting events in the kingdom.

"You know, fighting in Saudi for me is special and whatever it takes I'm going to be a world champion again," Canelo has said.

"Because I'm a fighter and I want to achieve a lot of things in boxing yet and that motivates myself. I love boxing."

Could Mbilli tarnish Canelo's legacy?

Matthew Hatton boxed Canelo back in 2011, in the first world title fight of the Mexican superstar's career. He thinks this fight could affect Canelo's legacy.

Sports.title: How Antonelli can win world title at Mexico City GP on Sunday
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City.

Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin to move 123 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate and nearest challenger George Russell, and 124 points ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris were officially knocked out of championship contention, leaving Russell and Hamilton as the only drivers who can technically prevent Antonelli from becoming the sport's youngest ever world champion at 20 years old.

In reality, Russell and Hamilton's chances are only technical, as one of them would need to win all five remaining races and for Antonelli to fail to score two points.

How Antonelli can win the 2026 F1 title at the Mexico City GP

There will be four scheduled races left - Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the Mexico City Grand Prix takes place this Sunday and a maximum of 100 points left to play for.

To win the title in Mexico City, Antonelli simply needs to score two points, or not be outscored by Russell by 24 points and Hamilton by 25 points.

The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Mexico City are:

Antonelli finishes ninth or better

Or

Russell and Hamilton fail to win the race

Antonelli will be champion if... Kimi Antonelli George Russell Lewis Hamilton 1st - - 2nd - - 3rd - - 4th - - 5th - - 6th - - 7th - - 8th - - 9th - - 10th 2nd or lower - 11th or lower 2nd or lower 2nd or lower

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'

When can Mercedes clinch the Constructors' Championship?

Mercedes will also have a first mathematical chance to clinch the Constructors' Championship in Mexico - but securing that title next time out is a very tall order.

They lead Ferrari by 133 points in the standings and there will be 172 points left to play for after this Sunday's race.

To become champions in Mexico, they would need to outscore Ferrari by 39 points. This would require Antonelli or Russell winning the Grand Prix, with the other driver in second or third, plus a disastrous race for both Ferrari drivers.

The Silver Arrows' first realistic chance to wrap things up will therefore likely come at next week's Sao Paulo Grand Prix when they would only need to finish the Interlagos event 129 points ahead, four fewer than now.

However, Ferrari have outscored them at each of the last three race weekends.

Sports.title: Sheff Utd win first league game against Wrexham in 44 years
Sports.content:
Sheffield United shook off a 44-year hoodoo by beating Wrexham 1-0 in the Championship, winning against the Welsh side in the league for the first time since October 1982.

It is a fixture that is turning in to one of the great EFL contests, but after their two Championship matches last term produced 11 goals, this one registered just five shots on target.

The majority were for the Blades, with Brentford loanee Romelle Donovan central to much of the good attacking play, although it was Ben Brereton Diaz who decided it.

He turned home a saved effort from Jordan Ayew for his third goal in three appearances against Wrexham, having scored in both games against them for Derby last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Brereton Diaz scored the winner for Sheffield United at Bramall Lane

Sheffield United should have had a penalty soon after after when Dominic Hyam fouled Harrison Burrows inside the area. However, the referee waved away the claims.

Sam Smith was introduced for Wrexham at the break and the Welsh side looked brighter after, but still only mustered one shot on target - coming in the 96th minute - as they extended their winless away run to five games.

Phil Parkinson cut a disappointed figure after the game, telling Sky Sports: "We haven't got that kind of Wrexham feeling in our performances where everybody's against us, everybody wants to beat us, we've got to fight harder and we've done it on several occasions, but not enough. You've got to do it every week."

The win sees the Blades move to within a point of the play-off places in 10th ahead of the remaining weekend games.

Wrexham remain in 17th with difficult fixtures against Middlesbrough and Wolves over the next eight days, although both are at home.

Wrexham have not kept a clean sheet in the Championship since a 0-0 draw against Swansea on September 5 - eight games ago. It is the first time they have gone eight games without a clean sheet since 2007 (19 years).

Parkinson: We have to look at ourselves closely and be honest

Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson to Sky Sports: "First half, we were second best all over the pitch. We've got to take a long look at ourselves for that because they were first to the ball, they were sharper, they closed down with more intent and as I always say to the lads, you know, I look at myself, but the performance in the first half was well below the standard.

"Coming to Bramall Lane, you've got to be ready for the intensity, being all over the pitch, winning your duels, your individual battles first and foremost to give you a foothold in the game.

"The second half was a lot better, but we're disappointed with that first 45 minutes because that wasn't how a Wrexham team plays or has played.

"We've got to turn up every week because it's a relentless division. Actually, you've got to turn up every week in any division and you've got to be ready.

"It's very easy in football to say 'oh the system, we should have done this', but let's look at ourselves first as individuals and could we have done better or were they just better than us? Were they just a better team than us or did they play in that first period with more hunger and desire? And we've got to look closely and be honest."

On the goal and if Anthony Patterson could have done better: "I honestly haven't looked at that back, but you can't criticise Patto for his performance tonight.

"He came and caught crosses, his handling was really good and sometimes a goalkeeper needs help in those situations, whether he could have partnered it around the post. I thought he put in a very solid performance."

Image: Sheffield United and Wrexham had just five shots on target between them

Wilder: Players picked up from second half vs Derby

Sheffield United boss Chris Wilder to Sky Sports: "The intent and approach was really good… I asked them to start the game as we finished it second half against Derby and they did. High up the pitch, got the press right.

"We understood that it was going to be a difficult second half. I've just said to the players, we're just a little bit loose on that first pass out.

"There was always going to be a reaction because they've won games of football for a long time and they're no mugs and they've got a real spirit about them. They had five or 10 minutes in the second half, we saw that out.

"We kept the ball and looked after the ball a little bit better then. They had nothing to lose, we had everything to lose. Sometimes you can have to defend and we did make a change late on. Michael [Cooper] has not had a lot to do in terms of saves."

Sheffield United have scored in their last six games in the Championship, their longest run of games with a goal in the competition since a run of 13 games from 24th January 2026 to 3rd April 2026.

On Ben Brereton Diaz: "I've known Ben for a long time. I know what his qualities are, I know what his character is like.

"I know where he started as a centre-forward in the early part of his career when he got his move to Blackburn. I've tracked his career right the way through. There's a lot of clubs in the division that were after him and delighted that he chose us.

"Not everybody hits the ground running. Not any player, whatever division they are, sometimes get themselves going but that'll do them no harm.

"I thought the performance of the two at the top of the pitch was really good, especially first half. They linked well, stretched well and the better team won the game of football."

Brereton Diaz: Good to get off the mark

Image: Brereton Diaz celebrates his winning goal

Sheffield United goalscorer Ben Brereton Diaz to Sky Sports: "It's nice to get off the mark. The lads were brilliant today from start to finish. We put a good shift in and we need to build on that. We go into a good week and then the international break is coming.

"I knew that I scored a couple against them last year so I hoped I could get one tonight and get off the mark. It's brilliant."

On backing from Chris Wilder: "The gaffer is unbelievable. This is my third time with him at Sheffield United. I love it here. The lads are unreal. It's a great place to be, we just need to build and everyone stay together."
