Sports.title: Brilliant Sun Goddess in class of her own at Breeders' Cup
Sports.content:
Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland.

Seen by many as the banker of the two-day meeting, she already had three Group Ones in Europe to her credit but she had to contend with the journey to America and stall nine.

However, Ryan Moore got her out of the stalls sharply and across to the inside in the perfect position just behind the leader whereas her main market rival, Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly, had to settle at the rear of the field.

As soon as Moore kicked clear early in the straight the race was over as a contest and once again it was left to Joseph O'Brien's Green Empress to chase her home, the fourth time she has been second to the winner this year.

Johnny Murtagh's Curracloe ran a fine race to finish third while Amusingly made late gains under Colin Keane for fourth. Joseph O'Brien's Alwaysanangel finished fifth in a clean sweep for the Europeans.

It was Aidan O'Brien's 22nd Breeders' Cup winner, meaning he has now had more winners at the meeting than anybody else, having been previously tied with Bob Baffert.

O'Brien said: "She was just really natural all the way from day one.

"She obviously had a run or two before Royal Ascot and she's taken everything in her stride.

"We could have taken in the Fillies' Mile in Newmarket on the way, and the lads just decided this with the view to next year. They wanted her here, so that's why she's here.

"Whether it's six furlongs, seven or even a mile now it all comes alike to her.

"Ryan just lets her come out and he lets her get comfortable in the first half and in the second half she comes home really well.

"I suppose a worry today was we all know what she can do when there's a strong pace on in front of her. He thought that he was going to end up a lot more forward than usual on her because he wasn't sure what was going to take her. So that's exactly what he did.

"I thought he gave her a beautiful ride. It was all very clean cut, no chances. The filly had a lovely day out.

"We usually start this kind of filly in the Guineas, I'd imagine the English Guineas is where she will start and there's a chance she might stay further."

Moore said: "What she's done this year is very unique, that is her fourth Group One from nine starts, that was her first over a mile though and the first time round a bend.

"There was a lot new to her but she was able to sit just off the pace and the pace was very ordinary really, we felt like we went a lot slower than we normally do in Cup races over a mile here.

"She was in front a long way from home and she was only idling really. It's hard to know where the bottom is for her. Hopefully she can continue next year."

Co-owner Michael Tabor said: "To win wherever the Breeders' Cup is held is very special because it's great competition and the crowds make it.

"I love American racing but it's tougher (to win) out here. Paul Shanahan buys so many of our horses and the irony of it is that this is maybe the cheapest (£120,000) he's bought but probably the best."

O'Brien went on to notch his 23rd Breeders' Cup success when Haffner claimed the Juvenile Turf.

Libertango delivers for Boughey and late sub Loughnane

Libertango came with a sustained late run under substitute jockey Billy Loughnane to win the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint at Keeneland.

In the days leading up to the race new UK champion jockey Loughnane had resigned himself to not taking the mount as her weight of 8st 7lb was 3lb lower than he had ridden at all season.

Loughnane could not face the prospect of seeing someone else take the mount, though, and having made a concerted effort in recent days to keep the weight off, one final stint in the sauna saw him meet the required point on the scales and trainer George Boughey was only happy to stand by his stable jockey.

Flavien Prat was the unlucky man to miss out, but bar meeting a slight but of trouble on the turn for home behind Andrew Balding's Moonrise, everything else went to plan.

Wesley Ward's Ruiva was the one to catch before Harper's Corner briefly hit the front only for Libertango to swamp them all. Adrian Keatley's Hell Of A Spin ran a massive race to get up for second.

Loughnane said: "I don't know what to say. I've ridden this filly in every single race and in every piece of work she's ever done and I thought I was going to have to give up the ride on her today.

"I've watched my weight for the last two weeks, obviously condolences to Flavien but I managed to just get enough off in the sauna and I'm sat on the smallest saddle I've ever ridden on. It's good to be able to get the weight off.

"It was awful thinking someone else was going to ride her but big thanks to George and all the team, it was literally 45 minutes before the race it was confirmed.

"She has such a good racing brain, she went to sleep. There was interference on the turn but she didn't even break stride and when I moved her out she hit the wire fantastic.

"I'm riding at 8st 10lb later on so I'd been aiming for that and I'd never been down to 8st 5lb all the time I've been riding, but it's a massive advantage having saunas here, we don't have them in England."

Boughey said: "Credit to Billy I didn't think he would do the weight but the saunas helped and it's the stuff of dreams. All credit to Billy as that was some ride.

"Flavien was meant to ride and it was a very late decision. Billy had ridden her all year and he text me when he got to the track saying he weighed in a lot lighter than he expected. I'd like to apologise to Flavien because he'd been booked a while and it was probably one of his better mounts of the day.

"The race look mapped out for her even from Royal Ascot. That was the plan to come here and for her to train as well as she did through the last few races, it wasn't a huge surprise that she was able to put in a performance like that today.

"The Breeders' Cup for me is as good as it gets. She's been ridden so beautifully by Billy all year. To say he wasn't riding her until 55 minutes before the race, he's just an extraordinary talent."

Sports.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar. “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.”

Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012, after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”.

Arteta was part of the Arsenal side that won at Anfield again six months later thanks to goals from the new signings Lukas Podolski and Santi Cazorla. That was the last time the club triumphed there in the Premier League. They have not won at Anfield for 13 league matches, equalling the club’s worst run at Liverpool. Arsenal’s one victory at Liverpool in the interim came in the League Cup on penalties in 2020 on Arteta’s second visit as a manager.

The Spaniard tried to prepare his players for a trip to Anfield in November 2021 by playing You’ll Never Walk Alone over the training ground speakers but that ended in a 4-0 defeat. He was criticised after last season’s loss in late August, when Dominik Szoboszlai’s late free-kick ended a sequence of three Arsenal draws at Liverpool, for a perceived failure to take off the handbrake, having started Mikel Merino as his No 10. Gary Neville went as far as to say Arsenal lacked “the mentality to go and win big matches at big away grounds”, an assertion that will have hurt Arteta but does have credence: they have not beaten Manchester City in the Premier League at the Etihad since 2015 under Arsène Wenger.

Arteta will be keen to disprove such perceptions, especially after Arsenal struggled so badly against a team 84 places below them in the pyramid in a stadium that holds fewer than 6,000 people. The strikers Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres surprisingly started in tandem at Fleetwood, presumably in an attempt to lighten the load on Martin Ødegaard, although both look badly out of form. Bukayo Saka is out with a thigh injury, there are concerns over Noni Madueke’s ankle and Arsenal’s failed appeal over Max Dowman’s red card rules out the teenager for three matches.

View image in fullscreen 26 May 1989: the Arsenal manager George Graham hugs Alan Smith after they won 2-0 at Anfield, clinching the league title in the most dramatic circumstances. Photograph: Mark Leech/Offside/Getty Images

With that in mind, Arteta’s best chance of beating Liverpool is probably by taking the cautious approach that has served him so well and was the cornerstone of last season’s Premier League title triumph. He can take inspiration from one of the most famous nights in Arsenal’s history 37 years ago when George Graham’s side arrived at Anfield needing a 2-0 victory to be champions.

“I told my players to keep things tight in the first half – it was imperative we did not concede,” said Graham in an interview to mark the 20th anniversary of that dramatic finale to the 1988-89 season, when Michael Thomas scored in stoppage time to end Arsenal’s 18-year wait for the title. “The papers were saying we’d have to attack from the off, but I was adamant that was wrong. If Liverpool had scored an early goal it would have been over. But they did very little attacking and played into our hands.”

Before the 1989 game, Arsenal’s players ran to all four corners of the ground to hand flowers to Liverpool fans as a show of sympathy after the Hillsborough disaster the previous month – an idea proposed by their longstanding director Ken Friar, who died this month.

Graham and Arteta were 44 when they won their first league titles and the similarities do not end there. The former Scotland midfielder, who scored almost 80 goals for Arsenal and helped them win the Double in 1971, was known for his emphasis on defending as a manager and “1-0 to the Arsenal” became synonymous with Graham, especially towards the end of his reign. Arteta has revived that tradition since he took over in December 2019, recording 1-0 victories 32 times in the Premier League, more than any club apart from Everton.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal of the season in a routine 2-0 win at home to Everton last Saturday and targeting Liverpool’s weakness from set plays while keeping things tight at the other end could be the most effective tactic against a team who have been finding their feet under Iraola in recent weeks.

“Collectively, we acknowledge the importance of defending,” said Arteta last year when asked about comparisons between his team and Graham’s. “We know that if we excel in that part of the game, the chances and the probabilities to win more matches is going to be very, very high.”

Arsenal flew back to London after losing to Fleetwood on penalties in a shootout that will have revived bad memories of May’s Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.

The Carabao Cup has stretched Arteta’s squad in the past two seasons, when they reached first the semi-finals then the final, so that is one potential positive from their elimination – not that the ultra-competitive Spaniard would agree. For him, the only way to respond to the most embarrassing night of his managerial career will be to follow in Graham’s footsteps on Sunday.

Sports.title: Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick said he has had difficult conversations with the Manchester United hierarchy and his players during their turbulent start to the season.

United have not won in their past eight games and start the weekend in 16th place of 20 in the league, one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position was under threat after losing last Sunday to Bournemouth but he has held on to his job for the time being and been given the chance to turn things around, starting at Chelsea on Saturday.

The head coach suggested he had spoken with the club’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the chief executive, Omar Berrada, this week.

“It’s pretty clear, it’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason, Omar or the owners,” Carrick said. “It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we will do.”

The supporters cheered Carrick off after he did a lap of the pitch in the aftermath of Sunday’s 3-0 defeat, but once he entered the tunnel they booed the players after a poor performance and perceived lack of effort. Carrick said the players are “hurting” but are “hungry” to turn things around.

“I’ll be totally honest, it was mixed feelings for me,” Carrick said. “To have the appreciation from the supporters and that connection and that respect is something I feel strongly about.

“It wasn’t a nice situation but to feel that was important, of course, but it didn’t make me feel better in the fact that I’m with the players 100% and we’re all in it together. I’ve told the players that, I’m happy to say that.

“I didn’t feel comfortable being in any way, shape or form, a separation from that. That’s my group, my players and this is my football club so we have to all be in it together, and that’s the supporters included. As hard as it is at the moment, I totally get that, I get their feelings, but when we get through this then we’ll be a lot stronger as a whole.”

Gary Neville questioned some of the players’ professionalism on his podcast this week. “I’ve got no time for them,” Neville said. “There’s a few of them that don’t go to bed at the right time. Don’t eat the right things.” Carrick laughed off the allegations with the remark: “Gaz says a lot of things.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for ‘unacceptable insults’
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters.

Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.

“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”

Former Liverpool defender Carragher made his remarks on the Stick to Football podcast while discussing the prospect of Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The 48-year-old Sky Sports pundit argued there was a hierarchy in football, saying “Aston Villa will never be Man United”.

“I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” said Carragher. “So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.

“But there will be teams below Aston Villa and they [Villa] will take their manager or they will take their players, so shut the fuck up Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United.”

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso rules out January loan move for Chelsea winger Estêvão Willian
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has ruled out a January move for Estêvão Willian but has said the Chelsea youngster must adapt to his style of play before earning a regular spot in the team.

The debate around Estêvão’s role gathered momentum this week, with the noise growing after the 19-year-old watched as an unused substitute as Alonso’s side lost to Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. The Brazilian became an instant hit with Chelsea fans after joining from Palmeiras last year and there are fears that the winger could look to leave after starting twice in 11 games in all competitions this season.

Yet while Estêvão is having a tougher time during his second year in English football, Alonso insisted that the Brazil international is part of his plans and will not be loaned out to get more games in January.

“No discussions about that,” Alonso said. “It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch. When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that. But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.”

There was a lot of hype around Estêvão after his £51.4m move. He impressed last season, particularly when he scored a brilliant solo goal against Barcelona, only for a hamstring injury to dash his hopes of going to the World Cup.

The teenager has struggled since returning from injury. Estêvão has played a total of 47 minutes in the Premier League this season. He earned an international recall from Carlo Ancelotti on Thursday but is yet to convince Alonso, who explained the process for Estêvão from a tactical perspective before Chelsea host Manchester United on Saturday.

“Well [it is] in the adaptation to the competition, the process to learn things with the ball, against the ball, how to be more competitive,” Alonso said. “That’s for all the players who have made that big step to the Premier League. I am part of the process to help him. For sure I understand the moment, I understand his feeling. It’s still early days.”

Alonso did not use all of his substitutions against Liverpool. He suggested physicality was a reason for Estêvão’s omission after the game. On Friday, Alonso said that improving without the ball is not the only issue.

“It’s one thing,” he said. “With the ball is very important as well. That’s sometimes when to take the right decision, what to do in the next situation. It’s to keep the ball, it’s to find the right pass. And, as well, against the ball you need to be competitive. That’s in football and in the Premier League mandatory now.

“The demand of the Premier League is higher than other leagues because of the tempo. To be there as a teenager is not easy. That’s why to go through this filter is not for everyone. It takes time. Even then there will be mistakes. Mistakes are part of the learning process.”

Alonso has often used a 3-4-2-1 system, with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers playing as No 10s. He considered whether Estêvão would be suited to a role in the middle.

“Depending on the game, the context, he could play more in this pocket position as a No 10,” he said. “But where he has played more in the Premier League has been as a winger. In one-on-one situations he has good moments.”

Chelsea have selection issues in defence before facing United. Jorrel Hato has a back problem and Maxence Lacroix is out until after the international break after sustaining a hamstring injury against Liverpool.

Sports.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry.

Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone.

This passage describes a moment where Gary plays a game having been urged by his friends to smoke pot beforehand to discover whether it improves his understanding of time and space, or just makes him want to lie down and untie someone’s laces. It marks a turning point for Gary. To this point football has been a comforting world. He sees clarity in its militaristic rituals, finds in sport “the illusion that order is possible”, hears hidden truths in the coaches’ shouted instructions. Button up. Get fetal. Get fetal. Get fetal. Run with reckless abandon.

Now the illusion has collapsed. Gary walks off the football field and begins instead to fixate on cold war fears and nuclear apocalypse. Death and political power have entered the chat.

Now, I’m not saying Marc Guéhi is Gary Harkness. You might be saying that. That’s your choice. But Guéhi has seemed a bit distracted in the last few weeks. Oddly for an agile and technically sound centre-back, he has seemed brittle and absent, vulnerable to being pressed.

There have been a couple of things said about City’s players in this regard. The first is that their minds might not be wholly on the game, that in the middle of a game against Croatia, for example, concerned only with manoeuvring through tiny pockets of space, Nico O’Reilly is also thinking: “Hmm, but how is it possible even by omission to honestly contravene rules E.3 and E.4 which state clearly that …oh. Wait, no. Oh dear.”

Football doesn’t work like this. The physical game is a place of total focus. But still, nothing is watertight. And this speaks to the second thing people have said, repeated like an absolute truth, that the players are entirely separate from all this. They cannot be questioned here, or indeed expected to ask questions of their own. The players are simply avatars, employees, free from any kind of agency. Players don’t have access to Google. They cannot make moral judgments. And yes, this may not be true of any other human in any other field. It may be the case that elite footballers are in fact unusually empowered, free to do whatever they want. But the consensus is clear. It is not a footballer’s business to have opinions on their employers, or what happens out of their line of vision.

This does help to avoid some tricky conundrums. Guéhi, for example, is a man of absolute public principle. Fair enough. I respect his willingness to resist popular pressure and personalise his support for the rainbow armband by writing things about Jesus on top of it. This is living your values. It’s free speech, figuring out your own moral universe. Doing so by following the absolute tenets of his religion. Go for it.

At the same time, Guéhi is playing for a club that has been convicted of cheating and lying. People are free to disagree with the rules. But if others are sticking to them, this amounts to deceit, stolen win bonuses, stolen glory. And the Bible is very clear on this. Thessalonians 4:6: “No one should transgress and defraud his brother.” Proverbs 20:17: “Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel.” Now, I don’t believe these words to be divinely ordained. They’re great words. Totally dig the vibe. But Guéhi does believe these things to be an absolute instruction. How does this fit together in his head? How does that gravel (pending appeal) taste right now?

View image in fullscreen The physical game is a place of total focus. But still, nothing is watertight. Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock

Again, fine if you can square it. It’s a personal journey. Park the apparent moral dilemma. See if your legal team can come up with a better final outcome. But things have changed in one significant way since the verdict dropped, an element that is now unchallenged, and which has been largely unremarked in the middle of the chaos. Understandably so. This stuff is gruelling. Everyone just wants to watch some football in the brief lull between legal rage events. But there are two points worth making in the interim. The second of which is an admission that affects many other things.

The first issue is: do you actually understand the basis of the Manchester City appeal? That evidence has seemingly been leaked. The irrefutable body of evidence, Body Of Evidence 2, the long-awaited tribunal-based Madonna erotic thriller vehicle, contains a vital detail: the additional money in City’s coffers, almost a billion, did not come from the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group, which is owned, like City, by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan. This would be against the rules. It came instead from the Abu Dhabi government, which is essentially the Abu Dhabi royal family, of which Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan is a member; as he is also, wearing a different hat, of the Abu Dhabi government.

And maybe this means it’s fine. It seems the government often tops up the sponsor companies like a benevolent uncle. In the period the charges relate to there was no need for sponsor deals to be of market value, as there is now. So if we accept all this, if we can establish a binding principle of wearing different hats in different rooms, this may be a way out. Maybe.

This is a familiar concept in the high court, in an age of shell companies and tricky fiscal flows. Mega-million cases hang on whether ownership really is separate, or whether this is, to echo a phrase, a sham process. The person on the Clapham omnibus might not buy any of this. Do these really seem like separate entities? Or a bit like adopting a French accent when the bailiffs ring up and maintaining that, no, Monsieur Ronay is not here, and he definitely doesn’t run this dry cleaners. That, instead, is me.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

If you make the case you win the case. This is all in the end about the application of rules, and that is a good thing. But the key point here is the secondary issue derived from this. City’s leaked defence, in making their case, is also saying, without pretence or mucking about, that the club is indeed funded by the Abu Dhabi government. This is something City’s fans have at times weirdly denied. But we have it in plain sight now, not just admitted but insisted on. The ultimate source of the dizzying success of the club that has defined a Premier League era is the government. Guéhi is, in effect, an Abu Dhabi civil servant. Perhaps the United Arab Emirates national team should have six stars on their jersey, one for each Premier League won. But there is no way of covering your ears now. City actively want us to accept this.

What are the consequences of this new fact? It comes with two urgent questions. The first is the moral one. Back again to Guéhi as the best example. This is what he is promoting here. And Guéhi is a man entirely guided by the principles of his faith. A private matter perhaps, except that it’s not, because Guéhi’s church explicitly orders its members to go out and proselytise. Guéhi is a member of Ballers in God, which actively tries to awaken Christian faith in the dressing room. He plays with Christian messages on his matchday kit intended to make you, the reader, think yes, maybe I too should follow this evangelical church.

And here is the key thing. This is a criminal offence in Abu Dhabi. Under UAE penal code, giving out Christian leaflets will get you arrested. A Christian pastor in the UAE was sentenced to a year in prison for giving a Muslim a Bible. Some Americans were deported for giving out Christian literature in the Dubai shopping district. Spreading the gospel, which Guéhi is morally bound to do, is illegal in the place that pays his direct employers.

Are players just avatars, empty shells? How much do you really believe in this? These are, more than ever, very interesting questions. And they don’t just apply to issues of personal principle.

The regulator now has this information, too. Abu Dhabi funded the purchase of Nolito. Abu Dhabi dictated the flow of English football finance. The same pocket that paid for this is also funding at arm’s length the civil war in Sudan, the hospital massacres, the piles of bodies so high they can be seen from satellite imaging. Abu Dhabi, which criminalises homosexuality, which crushes dissent, is openly identifying itself as the mega-funder of a Premier League club. Is this a fit and proper influence?

There are very obvious reasons why this is not desirable. Governments spy and wage war and break rules. They have a sacred trust to promote their own interests by any means necessary. It is hard to see how this kind of owner fits the regulatory framework. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund had to twirl through semantic hoops when buying Newcastle to establish it was an entity at one remove from a government, as opposed to a government entity. In making the opposite case for their funding City have not only exposed their own live-your-values central defender, they have put themselves in a place where, even if you win on one front, you’ve started to look like a very strange presence.

This deserves to be unravelled in all its wider implications. It may be the biggest issue here, whatever the final verdict. How can this be the right thing? How can City’s fans look their own autocratic government-funded club in the eye? The quiet thing has been said out loud. And its implications are bigger than the game, bigger than legal opinion. Enough, perhaps to make you question the existential point of this thing, where the best course of action really might be to walk off and look for the nearest cheeseburger.

Sports.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
Sports.content:
For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man.

That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “a breach of club discipline”.

Grealish is 31 and has 39 England caps. He is supposed to be a senior player but his career has involved far too many indiscretions. Breaking lockdown rules, a driving ban and more than once becoming a viral sensation for being pictured inebriated out and about have painted an unwanted picture. Learning from mistakes is part of life but Grealish’s indiscipline is apparently not dwindling with age. Guardiola warned him over his behaviour, dropping him in 2021 for a match against Newcastle after he and Foden arrived for training worse for wear.

Grealish is aware of his flaws, which is a starting point, but dealing with them is a separate matter. “People go: ‘He likes to go out, he likes to party,’ and I do,” Grealish told Sky Sports last year. “I want to be able to live my life and enjoy myself but obviously there’s a time and a place to do that. Sometimes, I’ll be honest with you, I probably haven’t picked the right times.”

Initially at Everton it seemed Grealish could be the poster boy of a new era. There were winners against Crystal Palace and Bournemouth by early December of last year and he had accumulated six assists in 20 Premier League appearances before his season was ended in mid-January by a foot injury. Grealish had been inconsistent, though. He has not played more than 28 league games in a season since 2019-20 at Aston Villa, which should concern him.

There were reservations at Everton about taking Grealish back this summer but Iliman Ndiaye’s sale to City made it a pragmatic move to fill the void. Grealish had carried out pre-season under Enzo Maresca, who gave him chances in the Community Shield and on the opening day against Bournemouth. The Italian had time for him but the unlikely redemption arc at City was soon quashed. Maresca showed affection for Grealish on Friday, saying: “I still think that he’s a good boy, big heart.”

View image in fullscreen David Moyes was terse on the subject of Jack Grealish and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond the length of his current loan. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

At his best, Grealish is a wonderful player, a carefree spirit when dribbling with his socks around his ankles. In full flow, he gets fans up off their seats, makes and takes goalscoring chances and forces opponents to foul him, but those moments have been fleeting for far too long. The next seven months are crucial to Grealish’s career; he is at an age where he could play at the top for years but his status is declining rapidly. He is a £100m City signing and treble winner but those are past glories. Grealish needs to prove he has the respect for himself and for Everton to want more.

Grealish’s contract at City concludes at the end of the season, so there is plenty of incentive for him to show he is capable of shining in the Premier League and inspiring Everton to the cup win they crave. Instead, his career is in limbo. David Moyes was terse on the subject of Grealish on Thursday and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond his loan. The Everton manager is working with a very small squad, so losing a senior player for avoidable reasons will surely frustrate and irritate him.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In an industry where the public is kept at arm’s length, Grealish is very approachable, happy to sign autographs for longer than his peers, eager to do the charity elements that come with playing for major clubs and known for his personal touch when others are businesslike. When entering and leaving Hill Dickinson Stadium, Grealish is mobbed, such is his popularity. He embraces it, posing for selfies with anyone who demands one, channelling a lot of positive energy into others, but he needs to find the self-awareness to do the same for himself.

“With me, I’m a big confidence player – I want to feel loved,” Grealish once said. He will not be feeling that from Moyes any time soon without radical change.

Sports.title: Suspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigation
Sports.content:
A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police.

It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award. Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outlet Upside’s investigation.

According to Raphaël Pautard, the co-founder of Upside, his team identified 12 Polymarket accounts created between 1 October and 20 October. The accounts displayed strikingly similar patterns of activity, leading investigators to suspect they could be connected to the same individual or group. Seven of the 12 accounts had not participated in any other betting markets, while six placed their first bets 15 minutes after being created.

Pautard revealed that his team managed to trace one transaction back to a French platform. After sharing the relevant blockchain transactions and wallet addresses with the company’s team, the platform reportedly confirmed it had identified the individual behind one of the accounts involved in funding the suspicious bets. The identity of that individual has not been publicly disclosed, but the development could prove significant in establishing connections between the accounts and tracing the money behind the wagers.

Quick Guide How do I 

Upside passed its findings to France Football, which Groupe Amaury owns and which has organised the awards since 1956. It is understood to have received confirmation on Friday afternoon that an investigation has been opened, with the French police also to be informed. France Football has been contacted for comment.

Rather than spreading their money across different outcomes, the accounts concentrated their wagers on a specific scenario: Kane winning, followed by Mbappé in second, Yamal in third, Rodri in fourth and Messi in fifth. Every position subsequently matched the official results, generating nearly $200,000 in profits.

According to the investigation by Upside, one account purchased a contract predicting Kane would win at 37 cents before selling it when the price reached 67 cents. The funds were subsequently redirected towards bets on specific finishing positions, including Yamal finishing third. This sequence of transactions has attracted attention because it suggests the account holder adjusted their strategy as the relevant markets developed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Before the ceremony, France Football had indicated that only a handful of people knew the winner in advance. The possibility that confidential information could have reached betting accounts before the official announcement is therefore a serious concern, particularly given the precision of the predictions and the amount of money involved. “How do we keep the winner’s identity hidden? I think a well-kept secret is one that is shared with as few people as possible,” said the former France Football editor Pascal Ferré last week.

Sports.title: Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage champions
Sports.content:
As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club’s Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or on Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday, two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d’Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, “awesome for the WSL”.

From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‑and‑a‑half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world’s best player has helped change the mindset of everyone at the club.

“Her impact on our commercial business is extraordinary,” he says. “From a leadership point of view, she allows us to start thinking about really winning. The environment today feels like it can beat Man City on Sunday and that’s a lot down to her.”

He acknowledges that Putellas, a World Cup winner with Spain and four-time European champion with Barcelona, and her brand – she has more Instagram followers (3.7m) than a men’s club the size of Porto, for example – were pivotal in helping the club secure what they claim is the largest front-of-shirt sponsorship deal in the women’s game, with Nike. The club say it is worth more than the new NWSL franchise Atlanta’s sponsorship of $4m (£3m) a year.

“It’s insanely big,” Semmens says. “Our view on how to run this business, rightly or wrongly, was to invest first, invest in the everything to make it awesome, and then the commercial deal will be big. The other way, of: ‘Let’s sit back, let’s grow a fanbase, let’s wait for the money to come’ – we don’t have the patience for that. Michele’s vision was: ‘I’m going to invest now to prove that we can bring these deals in.’ That deal allows us to kick forward, it allows us to keep investing in players and infrastructure, because without it, we’re just burning Michele’s money, which is not the plan.”

Even with Kang’s money, signing a player who had been loyal to Barcelona for 14 years was never going to be straightforward. Semmens, the former Southampton chief executive, says: “The conversation went: ‘Wait until I’ve finished winning a Champions League with Barcelona and then we’ll have a conversation,’ which we loved and we respected, but we always had a feeling she would come.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas has provided a huge commercial lift to the club. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

“I think she had bought into four or five significant things. One, that we are independent, we’re a women’s-first environment. [Two] there’s a lot of power in coming to London, as a city. The WSL is important – people see WSL as the growth brand. And, after that, Michele had an unbelievably massive impact [on Putellas’s decision]. Alexia said to me: ‘Well, she said she was going to do all this stuff and she’s done it. So I want to be part of that.’ And then also, it allows her to have a legacy in the future – she will grow this club to a point where she’s creating a pathway for the next young players to come through in London.”

There are questions facing the club in relation to how much they have been spending and eyebrows were raised – to put it mildly – around the rest of the league when London City recorded an operating loss of more than 10 times their revenue for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion as second-tier champions. Since then salary cap rules have been introduced in the WSL, stating no club’s player wage bill can exceed the following figures combined: 80% of revenue, plus up to £4m or a further 25% of revenue (whichever is higher).

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas’s arrival has undoubtedly put London City Lionesses on the map. Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Last season, when London City finished sixth, the league’s handbook said no punishments would be dished out for any breaches of that cap for that campaign only. From this term, points deductions could apply, which is one reason why it was imperative to increase commercial revenues. But were they within the rules last term?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We are 100% within the rules, we will always be,” Semmens says. “It’s so important to Michele.” He says the “goal of the business” is to be profitable within five years and likens last year’s investments to a “start-up fund”: “The [salary cap] rules were set up with a clear understanding that they wouldn’t come until this year. The handbook is 100% clear. We want to see investment coming into the women’s game. Anything that kind of restricts positive and good investment obviously worries [me] but there is a need for rules and we’re 100% fine with that. We are super-transparent. We can reassure the fans that we are financially viable, sustainable, and we’ve made serious investments over the last two years to be profitable and successful in the future.”

Another question facing the club, particularly given their league position, is whether they would be eligible to compete in the Women’s Champions League, given Kang also owns the record eight-time European champions OL Lyonnes in France. Semmens says in reference to Uefa’s multi-club ownership rules: “One hundred per cent, it can be resolved. We will continue to argue the case that you should be able to [invest into multiple clubs] to see the women’s game accelerated.“It’s not about exchanging players like the men’s game. It’s not about one club dominating and the other being a feeder club. It’s a different model but we fully understand and respect the rules. Therefore, we will set ourselves up in a way where we’re allowed to and can compete in Europe together. There are clear rules, clear precedents in the men’s game and clear things you can do to allow both teams to flourish. We’re fully aware of that and we’ll comply with the rules.”

London City are three points off Chelsea and Manchester City, and Semmens says the aim is to “build a squad that is consistently in the top three”. He is looking forward to Sunday. “This is probably the No 1 game in the women’s game in the world this weekend,” he says. “That’s what we want to be: on the map.”

Sports.title: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson SPLIT: NFL icon, 74, and cheerleader girlfriend, 25, have 'called it quits... and she already has a new man'
Sports.content:
NFL legend Bill Belichick and his cheerleader girlfriend Jordon Hudson have called it quits and are no longer dating, according to a bombshell new report.

In fact, TMZ claims the high-profile pair called time on their age-gap romance late last year – and Jordon has even begun dating new men.

The outlet reports that they are 'still close friends and remain committed to their business partnerships,' despite their secret split.

The legendary former New England Patriots coach, 74, started dating the cheerleader, 25, back in 2022, after they first met on a flight from Boston to Florida.

They were first pictured together in January 2023, before finally going public with their relationship in June 2024.

They have since been on a whirlwind and often controversial romance, which resulted in them living together between North Carolina, where Belichick is currently coaching the UNC football team, and Nantucket.

Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson secretly ended their age-gap relationship last year, per TMZ

The pair were spotted beaming on the sideline of a UNC game as recently as this month

Hudson has been an ever-present at Belichick's side despite reports of their romance ending

A source close to Hudson told TMZ that the pair quietly ended their relationship 'late last year,' though it is unclear who exactly pulled the plug.

It is also being reported that Hudson has been 'seeing other people' since her romance with Belichick, who is 49 years her senior, came to an end.

The Daily Mail has reached out to the pair for further comment.

It is extremely surprising that the news wasn't made public any earlier, especially given Hudson has been a constant presence on the sideline at UNC games this season – and as recently as last weekend against Syracuse in Chapel Hill.

A week earlier, she was alongside her now-ex-boyfriend for the road game against Duke, with the pair beaming as they left the field together.

It remains to be seen whether Hudson will resume her role on the sideline in the wake of their split becoming public knowledge, with UNC at home against No 1-ranked Miami in Chapel Hill on Saturday night.

Bizarrely, the pair were also seen holding hands during a public appearance at the Kentucky Derby in May, after which Hudson posted a photo with the caption: 'Not the first time we’ve trudged through the mud together,' with a love heart.

Hudson and Belichick are regularly at each other's sides despite reports of a secret split

While it is reported they split last year, the pair held hands at the Kentucky Derby in May

That trip came months after their reported split at the end of 2025.

During the course of their romance, Hudson amassed an impressive $9 million property portfolio, as first reported by the Daily Mail.

She has snapped up at least four properties, including one worth $3 million, which were all purchased after she met the former New England Patriots coach.

Even more impressively, she has also paid off the mortgages on each of the homes, with her primary residence listed as a two-bedroom cottage in Cape Cod.

Records also show that she has registered 18 companies – several with names that suggest she had, or has, some control over Belichick's affairs.

She had been operating as Belichick's de facto manager during their relationship, and it appears she is still involved with him from a business perspective if not a romantic one.

Her control of his affairs hit the headlines most notably during a CBS Sunday Morning interview back in April 2025.

Belichick celebrates with his UNC players after winning on the road against Duke on October 17

Hudson, sitting out of shot, muscled in on reporter Tony Dokoupil's line of questioning about how the pair met, shouting out: 'We're not talking about this.'

CBS broadcast the multiple interruptions made by Hudson throughout the interview, with TMZ later reporting that she 'walked out and delayed filming by 30 minutes' and at one point even corrected Belichick while he was discussing football.

More recently, Belichick was forced to deny that Jordon has been 'trying to control UNC's football program,' calling the claims 'ridiculous' in an interview with the Wall Street Journal in September.

To reports she is involved in virtually everything he does, Belichick responded that that is a 'flat-out lie.'

Prior to his relationship with Hudson, Belichick was married to his ex-wife Debby for 30 years, before they separated prior to the 2004 NFL season.

He was then in a long-term relationship with girlfriend Linda Holliday for approximately 16 years, from 2007 to 2022.

Sports.title: Fallon Sherrock BEATS Luke Littler to win £501k in Netflix challenge: 'Queen of the Palace' holds back tears after winning in front of her son - seven years on from fairytale World Championship run
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock made more history on Friday night as she defeated Luke Littler to take home a life-changing £501,000 on Netflix's Beat Luke Littler.

It took Sherrock, who has won two matches at the World Championship previously – her first win seeing her become the first female player to win at the tournament – 14 darts to claim victory, and her son rushed onto the stage to embrace her and her new fortune.

'It's insane,' she said, fighting back the tears. 'I can't put into words how much this means. And having my son, the first time he's ever been to anything, and he saw me win.

'It was lovely. Sorry, I'm lost for words. It was a great moment and I'll remember it forever. Give me an opportunity and I'll take it every time. I'm really proud of myself right now.'

Littler said: 'That's what one person had to do. I wanted her to give me a chance, and she didn't.

'I've enjoyed every minute of it. It's been good.'

The moment Fallon Sherrock hit a 180 before going on to #BeatLukeLittler and win £501k! pic.twitter.com/jrpkPvWBFw — Netflix UK & Ireland (@NetflixUK) October 30, 2026

Luke Littler was defeated on Netflix on Friday night as Fallon Sherrock claimed £501,000

Sherrock needed just 14 darts to beat the two-time world champion and take home the prize

It was first assumed that the common man or woman would be taking on Littler for the chance at life-changing money. Netflix's  featured people lining up to audition that no one had ever seen before.

More than 3,000 people auditioned in London and Manchester to take on The Nuke. Hopefuls travelled from far and wide, queuing from the early hours of the morning.

And so fans were left puzzled when the line-up was announced. Among them were semi-pro stars, upcoming hotshots, and even players who have competed at the World Championship before.

Queen of the Palace Sherrock, six and soon to be seven-time Ally Pally participant, once reaching the last-32 in 2019; Wee Sox Mitchell Lawrie, the reigning World Darts Federation Youth champion and World No1; Fierce Pearse Mackle, who has played youth darts for Ireland; Young Gun Jayden Walker, 14, who has played Littler before - and he wasn't the only one. Others who have played at semi-pro level.

'I don't need the money,' Sherrock told Daily Mail Sport at the London auditions. 'But I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you?

'I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

Some felt short-changed. Some have indeed come from nowhere – a teacher, a Nando's restaurant manager and a business adviser were all featured – but the selection process hardly went down as Netflix would have hoped.

Littler 'put his reputation on the line', Gary Lineker told us as the show started.

Up to 20 hopefuls would be given the chance to face Littler, with Sherrock compeititor No 15

On the punditry team, alongside darts player and analyst Laura Turner was Richard Osman, Littler's friend Angry Ginge and comedian Lee Mack. We then saw Joe Marler and Josh Denzel. Darts.

Qualifiers were ranked and put into pots. Sixteen players were seeded, then others were wildcards who the public would vote for in a one-off contest.

Mack, frankly, had no idea. He asked if anyone had played at a high standard. What happened if Littler was beaten early. Said that more Professional Darts Corporation matches should bull up. They do.

Cheerleaders followed Littler to stage, which was where he stayed for the duration of the night. A hug for girlfriend Faith. Were the nerves starting to hit?

First up was 16-year-old Kasey Smith. Or 'Katie', according to Lineker. Smith was left stranded on 261, but did herself no shame. One down.

Tony Cole had never played against anyone before. He got closer, but not really close at all. Two down.

The major disadvantage that the challengers had was that Littler was regularly winning the bull, meaning he threw first in the leg. Playing against the darts is always a challenge – it's worse when facing the best in the world.

Zach the professional jockey – who entered with a horse – fell short despite putting up a solid competition. Olly Murs was then interviewed. Again, darts.

Sherrock's family celebrated in the crowd and would eventually join her on stage in Manchester

She was presented with a cheque - having previously told Daily Mail Sport she 'doesn't need the money'

Jayden Walker could have provided serious competition up next. He has broken some of Littler's youth records and got the better of Luke Humphries before. Here, he had no answer as Littler pinned his first 180 and checked out 158 to win.

The first wildcard selection felt awkward. Two hopefuls stood at the end of the walk-on – one, decided by a live viewer vote, walked forward. The other headed backstage. What a waste of time.

And 18-year-old bin man Taylon Forrester came close. The crowd began to boo Littler's throw. He came through his toughest challenge yet as his opponent got down to a finish.

The next, Mackle, had a dart at the bull. His life flashed before his eyes. Netflix were more interested in getting Olly Murs on screen than actually filming the dart, but he missed. Littler didn't. 'I'm happy enough with that,' Mackle said. The closest we'd come by far.

Fifty-seven-year-old Mark Pooke hit a 12-dart leg in the auditions. He won the bull, but then threw away the advantage and seemed to lose his bottle. Stone faced, but Littler prevailed against the No2 seed.

Littler's average at this point had dropped into the 80s. Though a second ton-plus out shot took him to ten wins.

'It's tough when it's constant,' Littler said. 'Anyone can cause me bother.'

Littler hit only two 180s. He wasn't good enough, or he didn't need to? Pick your narrative.

Sherrock won the bull as challenger number 15. The trebles started to come. She left 43. Littler a mile away.

The roof came off the place. Fallon Sherrock made history again. Her son rushed onto stage. She may not be the best player – or even the best female player – but she has a habit of making history.

And so Littler was beaten by Sherrock, who, for some reason Lineker said at the close 'arrived as a hairdresser from Milton Keynes'.

'Let's do it again next year,' The Nuke said. It's back to making the millions for him now.

Sports.title: Aston Villa threaten legal action against Jamie Carragher after pundit claimed Unai Emery should replace Michael Carrick at Man United and told fans to 'shut the f*** up'
Sports.content:
Aston Villa threaten legal action against Jamie Carragher after pundit claimed Unai Emery should replace Michael Carrick at Man United and told fans to 'shut the f*** up'

Aston Villa last night made the bombshell claim that they intend to take legal action against Jamie Carragher.

In a statement on club channels carrying the name of co-owner Nassef Sawiris, Villa wrote: ‘Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

‘Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.’

Television pundit Carragher believes Emery would be the ideal manager of Manchester United if they decided to sack Michael Carrick.

That has prompted a furious response from Villa fans on social media.

Carragher doubled down on his view on The Overlap podcast this week, in which he told ‘Aston Villa fans’ to ‘shut the f*** up.

Aston Villa have decided to launch legal action against Jamie Carragher in a row over his comments about Unai Emery

‘I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

'But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

Sports.title: Emiliano Martinez reveals his finger 'won't ever return' to normal after injury left him playing like  a 'zombie' during World Cup: 'I cried every day'
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup. Martinez broke and dislocated a finger in the warm-up before playing for Aston Villa in their Europa League final triumph over Freiburg in May. The 34-year-old told Argentine journalist Gaston Edul’s YouTube channel that he cried after seeing x-rays having feared he would be ruled out of Argentina's World Cup title defence. After receiving support from Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, Martinez explained a decision was taken to avoid undergoing surgery that would have ruled him out of the tournament. Martinez was instead provided with a special glove from Adidas to protect the injured finger, which he admitted meant he could not grasp the ball properly. 'It will never go back to how it was,' Martinez said. 'I am still playing with pain.' Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup. Source: YouTube/Gastón Edul Martinez sustained a broken finger before playing for Aston Villa in the Europa League final The shot stopper wore a special glove from Adidas to protect his injured finger to ensure he could play at the World Cup, but admits he will need surgery in the future 'The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie. 'If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage. 'But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again.' Martinez added that a summer transfer to Italy – with Juventus having targeted the star – ultimately collapsed as a direct result of the injury. 'I got an x-ray and it was broken again,' Martinez said. 'That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger. 'They said it was possible for me to play like that, that I needed surgery, but Chelsea didn't, they didn't care. One day I will need surgery.' Martinez, who joined Chelsea for £7.5million in the summer, is currently recovering from a broken jaw sustained in their victory over Everton earlier this month.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits back at Gary Neville after his former Man United team-mate accused players of being unprofessional - and opens up on crunch meeting with struggling stars
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits back at Gary Neville after his former Man United team-mate accused players of being unprofessional - and opens up on crunch meeting with struggling stars

Michael Carrick has rejected claims that his Manchester United stars have been unprofessional, and vowed to stand by them in the face of fierce criticism from pundits and fans.

Carrick’s former teammate Gary Neville accused some players of not going to bed at the right time or keeping to a healthy diet, while Wayne Rooney said they need ‘a firework up their a**e’ for the performances that have left their head coach fighting to save his job.

United fans turned on the team following Sunday’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford, applauding Carrick down the tunnel before immediately venting their anger at the players.

Asked if he has encountered the unprofessional behaviour insinuated by Neville, Carrick said: ‘No, I haven’t. Gaz says a lot things!’

After United decided to give their head coach more time to turn the season around, he met with the players when they returned to Carrington on Tuesday and spoke about the backlash from fans.

‘Just to be clear, it was more for them to understand that I'm right in there with them. There's no way that I'm separated from that,’ said Carrick ahead of Saturday's crucial game at Chelsea.

Gary Neville (left) said Man United players were 'unprofessional' but Michael Carrick (right) insists he is standing by them in the face of criticism

‘As much as I totally respect and appreciate the response from the supporters, I'm right there with them and we'll go through this together.

‘It was mixed feelings for me. To have the appreciation from the supporters and that connection and that respect is something I feel strongly about.

‘It wasn't a nice situation, but to feel that was important, of course. But it didn't make me feel better in the fact that I'm with the players 100 per cent.

‘We're all in it together and I've told the players that. I'm happy to say that. I didn't feel comfortable being separated from that in any way, shape or form.

‘That's my group, they're my players and this is my football club, so we have to all be in it together.

‘That includes the supporters. As hard as it is at the moment, I totally get that. I get their feelings. When we get through this, we'll be a lot stronger as a whole.

‘We need to play better and we need to show certain things better. But the connection with us is as strong as ever.’

The fans also targeted United’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

On his meeting with the players, Carrick added: ‘It's pretty clear. It's not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that's between me and the players, whether that's between me, Jason or Omar or the owners. It's the hard truth at times and it's what we need to move forward.’

Sports.title: Man United interested in Barcelona star Fermin Lopez as they look to bolster attack after Benjamin Sesko injury blow
Sports.content:
Manchester United have shown an interest in Barcelona’s attacking midfielder Fermin Lopez as they look to add to their goalscoring options in the next transfer window.

The Spain international, 23, is rated in the £70million bracket and is also coveted by Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea after netting five times for the Catalans this season.

Lopez was ruled out of last summer's World Cup triumph with a foot injury. However, he has long had admirers at Old Trafford, even if there is an acknowledgement that United’s finances may be an issue.

The club have been linked with Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin this week, a player they looked at but didn’t move for during his last year at Everton.

United fear their Slovenian striker Benjamin Sesko could be out until at least January with a shin injury and desperately need cover for the 23-year-old, as manager Michael Carrick is left without a recognised centre-forward.

Daily Mail Sport understands a move for Calvert-Lewin is viewed as difficult given the fierce rivalry between the two clubs.

Fermin Lopez is rated at £70million and is also coveted by Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea

Calvert-Lewin has revitalised his career at Leeds after joining on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, following an injury-plagued end to his time at Everton.

The England striker is also believed to be discussing a new deal at Elland Road, such has been his impact. The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for Leeds, including five in ten games at the start of this season.

United will also look at defenders in January if any spare funds are found.

Sports.title: NFL press conference descends into farce as Cardinals star Budda Baker responds to trade talk... while refusing to take off his Halloween mask
Sports.content:
Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker turned heads on Friday when he was quizzed by reporters about his NFL future... while dressed in a full Halloween costume.

The bizarre press conference, perhaps unsurprisingly, quickly went viral and fans were left split by the football star's decision to not take off his mask for reporters.

Seemingly trying to add some fun to an often-monotonous moment for the players, Baker was perhaps not expecting to field some hard-hitting questions from the journalists in the room.

In a clip that has now been viewed over a million times, a reporter asks: 'I know you talked about this a little bit earlier in the week, but obviously, as we near the trade deadline, your name seems to be a name that pops up here and there on speculation. How do you look at that? How do you think about all that stuff?'

Opting against lifting his mask to speak more freely about a potential life-changing decision, Baker speaks through his scary face-mask, noting: 'Yeah, just live in the present. You know, like today, having a great time with you guys.

'Gonna have a great Friday practice, and just focus on playing against the Dallas Cowboys and trying to get a W at their stadium.'

Budda Baker opted against taking off his Halloween costume to answer reporters' questions

Baker has been the subject of trade speculation as the November 10 deadline fast approaches

Baker is an eight-time Pro Bowl safety that has been linked with the exit door in Arizona ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

Earlier in the week, he told ESPN that he had not requested a trade, nor had he had any discussions with general manager Monti Ossenfort about his future.

Multiple reports had linked Baker with an exit, as he continues on the second year of the three-year, $54 million contract he signed in December 2024.

He is scheduled to earn $16.17 million this season, and expects to be in the lineup to face the Cowboys on Sunday.

On social media, meanwhile, fans weren't sure how to react to Baker's bizarre mask, with some slamming him for not taking his career seriously, while others sided with him and claimed it was a hilarious move to add some levity to the media session.

'He wins the internet today,' one wrote, while another added: 'This is a different level of hilarious.'

One critic claimed: 'Clown. Not about it. Joke franchise,' while another told Baker he was a 'loser' for the stunt.

Sports.title: Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or by one of the smallest margins EVER: Full results are revealed after England captain's triumph
Sports.content:
Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or by one of the smallest margins EVER: Full results are revealed after England captain's triumph

Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe by a slender 28 point margin to be crowned as winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Kane claimed football's ultimate individual honour on Monday night, becoming the first Englishman to win since Michael Owen in 2001.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern Munich and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded Bayern Munich's domestic Treble, while he also captained England to third place at the World Cup.

A full breakdown of the results has now been revealed, with Kane topping the vote by receiving 1,055 points from an international jury of 100 journalists.

Mbappe, who had also been seeking to win the award for the first time in his career, finished agonisingly short with the Real Madrid and France star receiving 1,027.

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by just a 28-point margin, the full vote breakdown has revealed

Kylian Mbappe narrowly missed out on winning the award for the first time in his career

The gap is shorter than the closely fought battle between Rodri and Vinicius Jr in 2024, with the Spaniard having triumphed on that occasion by just 41 points.

HOW THE TOP TEN RANKED 1. Harry Kane, 1,055 points 2. Kylian Mbappé, 1,027 points 3. Lamine Yamal, 881 points 4. Rodri, 726 points 5. Lionel Messi, 612 points 6. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, 541 points 7. Ousmane Dembélé, 418 points 8. Erling Haaland, 378 points 9. Michael Olise, 296 points 10. Fabian Ruiz, 201 points

Lionel Messi's 2019 triumph over Virgil van Dijk is the narrowest margin of recent votes, with just seven points separating the pair.

Previously Matthias Sammer beat legendary Brazilian forward Ronaldo to the honour in 1996 by one point, with the same margin also seeing Sir Bobby Charlton beating Eusebio in 1966, when just 22 people voted.

In total, 40 of the voters had ranked Kane as their top choice, earning him 15 points each time, with Mbappe receiving 23 first place votes by comparison.

Kane was left out of the top ten by two journalists, while three overlooked Mbappe.

Lamine Yamal, who was widely viewed as a front-runner for the award alongside Kane and Mbappe, ultimately ended 174 points behind the winner.

Rodri and Messi completed the top five having earned 726 and 612 points respectively.

Since 2022, the current system is based on voting by a large panel of international journalists from the top 100 FIFA-ranked countries, and top 50 for the Ballon d'Or Feminin. Only a single journalist from each country in these rankings is given a vote.

Lamine Yamal ultimately ended in third place in the vote, finishing 174 points behind Kane

Kane and his wife Kate Goodland shared a kiss after he won the striker award (left) and Ballon d'Or (right) on Monday night

Each journalist must establish a ranking of top ten players from a list of 30 named players also designated by France Football.

A first place vote is worth 15 points, with the number reducing until tenth position, where players secure one point.

Voters are asked to take into account individual performances and their decisive and impressive character.

They are then requested to consider their collective role and the trophies won, before weighing up a player's class and fair play.

Kane had celebrated on Monday night with friends and family, including his wife Kate, after receiving the award at the London Palladium.

Kane made sure to pay tribute to Kate, who he married in 2019, after seeing off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to win.

He said: 'To my wife, Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself.

'The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you.

'This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you.

'Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.'

The couple share two daughters, Ivy and Vivienne, and two sons, Louis and Henry.

And Kane also made sure to reference them in his acceptance speech at the glitzy ceremony at the London Palladium.

'My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped,' he said. 'So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

The couple are both from Walthamstow and Kate has been the rock by her husband's side for years.

Kate is a sports science graduate and professional fitness coach, with 382k followers on Instagram.

The couple posed for photos on the red carpet at the London Palladium Theatre

Kane proposed in the Bahamas in 2017 and they married two years later, now living happily in Bavaria where they have settled well since the striker elevated his game to another level, dominating the Bundesliga.

During his emotional address on stage, he also thanked his parents. He said: 'Wow, wow, wow. I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight.

'Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough this year. Mum and dad, what a moment. All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you're there.

'All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.'

And Kane got royal approval as he hit the summit of world football's personal awards from Prince William.

'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or!' William wrote in a post on Instagram. 'What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or scores published as Harry Kane's slender winning margin revealed
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or scores published as Harry Kane's slender winning margin revealed

Harry Kane claimed the Ballon d'Or on Monday night but the Bayern Munich star's margin of victory was a minor one as he edged out Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe

View 2 Images Harry Kane won his Ballon d'Or by just 28 points (Image: Jeff Spicer - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by just 28 points with his narrow margin of victory over Kylian Mbappe being published.

‌



‌



The Bayern Munich ace won the individual accolade for the first time in his career on Monday and also ended a 25-year wait for a English winner as he scooped the gong in his hometown, London.

‌



Heading into the ceremony there was talk of a unique three-way battle for the award as Kane, Mbappe and Lamine Yamal all had genuine cases to claim the Ballon d'Or. Kane would win ahead of the Frenchman, but the contest was particularly close. Kane amassed 1,055 points with Mbappe just behind on 1,027.

‌



For all the talk of a three-way battle, Yamal was a distant third with 881 points. The World Cup winner's exploits were not enough to see him claim the award.

It is worth noting that the journalists who represented Spain and Germany both handed their vote to Mbappe - not the players who play in their domestic league.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

For Mbappe it was the best showing of his career to date. He'd previously finished third in 2018 following his World Cup victory with France, but topped that after delivering the best goalscoring season of his career - leading charts in La Liga, the Champions League and at the World Cup.

‌



His trophyless season may well have counted against him with Kane helping Bayern continue their German dominance - winning the league and cup double. He also got the better of Mbappe when England beat France to third at the World Cup.

From third to tenth the margins were relatively comfortable with few players close to going up or down the rankings. Rodri in fourth, Lionel Messi in fifth and seventh-placed Ousmane Dembele are the last three winners of the Ballon d'Or.

‌



View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe narrowly missed out on the Golden Ball

Kane said after his victory: “Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year. Some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my team-mates and world-class players in the room tonight, so thank you to everyone who voted for me.

‌



"Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight - an impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done."

Ballon d'Or top 10

1. Harry Kane, 1,055 points

‌



2. Kylian Mbappé, 1,027 points

3. Lamine Yamal, 881 points

‌



4. Rodri, 726 points

5. Lionel Messi, 612 points

‌



6. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, 541 points

7. Ousmane Dembélé, 418 points

‌



8. Erling Haaland, 378 points

9. Michael Olise, 296 points

10. Fabian Ruiz, 201 points
