Sports.title: Leclerc puts Ferrari on top in practice again in Mexico | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc started the Mexican Grand Prix on top by setting the fastest time in the opening practice session.

It was the fourth consecutive practice session headed by a Ferrari, after the team led all three sessions in Austin a week ago.

The two Mercedes drivers came next, Andrea Kimi Antonelli leading Frederik Vesti, who took over from George Russell. Vesti lapped within a tenth of a second of the driver who can clinch the world championship on Sunday.

The majority of teams ran junior drivers in the opening practice session. Behind Lewis Hamilton, Ayumu Iwasa set the quickest time by any driver who did not use the soft tyres. Isack Hadjar in the other Red Bull ended the session outside the top 10 after being delayed by a power unit problem.

Pierre Gasly took sixth while Fernando Alonso put his Aston Martin much further up the times sheets than usual with the seventh-fastest time.

Oscar Piastri, the quickest McLaren driver, was only eighth. Leonardo Fornaroli, replacing Lando Norris for this session, struggled to brake as aggressively as he needed to at turn one, running wide during his soft tyre run.

Oliver Bearman and Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Formula 2 driver Nikola Tsolov became the first Bulgarian driver to participate in an official practice session and impressed by lapping a tenth of a second slower than the team’s regular driver.

Other newcomers had less smooth sessions. Audi sent Freddie Slater out of the garage with a fan assembly in his right-hand sidepod. He had to pit to have it removed, then return to the garage for a longer stay due to overheating. The stewards are investigating the team’s unsafe release of the car.

Jak Crawford, driving Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin, parked up with a technical problem after leaving the track at turn one.

Colton Herta ended the session at the bottom of the times but passed an important milestone. Completing 30 laps ensured he will reach the 40 superlicence points he needs in order to be allowed to race in Formula 1.

Sports.title: ‘There’s no pay drivers now’: Alonso’s rivals reject his criticism of ‘one-third’ of the grid | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso’s rivals do not share his view that one-third of the Formula 1 grid has “very low” driving standards.

The Aston Martin driver’s comments were prompted by his first-lap tangle with Alexander Albon in the United States Grand Prix last week. “I think the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment,” the two-times world champion remarked.

Albon initially tried to downplay his rival’s comments as being made “in the heat of the moment” after the race. But Alonso stood by his criticism of the Williams driver’s first-lap lunge, saying he didn’t understand why Albon thought his attempt to pass on the inside of turn 11 would work.

However Albon maintained he disagreed with Alonso and defended the standard of driving in F1, claiming it is higher now than in past seasons when more drivers bought their way onto the grid.

“I have huge respect for Fernando,” said Albon. “I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid.

“Obviously, it’s not nice to hear those comments in many ways. You’re racing someone that you looked up to, but at the same time, I don’t agree. It’s as simple as that.

“I think the level is strong up and down the grid. Ten or fifteen years ago, the back half of the grid wasn’t the way it is now. You don’t have pay drivers anymore. It is what it is, hopefully we don’t cross paths in the race this weekend.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Pierre Gasly, who is in his tenth season in F1, agreed the standard of driving has improved.

“You have to love Fernando for the statements he makes out there,” said the Alpine driver. “I have so much respect for the driver he is, and at the same time, he’s very vocal.

“I’m not too sure – I haven’t seen his race, I’m not too sure what he referred to – but I think I would agree. I will say that the level on the grid is probably one of the highest, considering all the drivers we have now, from what I’ve seen over maybe nine years. I’ve seen some wild driving approaches when I joined compared to what I see now.”

Oliver Bearman, who is 13th in the championship, said those in the bottom half of the field need to take more risks to stand a chance of scoring points.

“Luckily, I’m just about in the middle third, not the bottom one, so I get away with it,” he said. “But no, I think that’s a slightly harsh conclusion.

“I agree with Pierre that the level is very high on this current grid. With the gaps that we face this year, you have to be very opportunistic at times, and that can end in disaster, like it did for me last week with myself and Pierre.

“So I wouldn’t say it’s a question of quality. It’s a question of trying your very best and trying to make something happen, which is very challenging when the top eight positions are pretty much all filled by the top four teams.”

Sports.title: ‘Not much more I could have done’ about ‘horrible’ title defence – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says he’s happy to see Andrea Kimi Antonelli succeed him as world champion because he’s performed so well this year.

The reigning world champion is no longer in contention to win the title again this year. Antonelli is virtually guaranteed to win the world title this weekend.

Norris, who prevailed in a three-way fight in the final round of last season to take the title, said “I don’t really care” that Antonelli faces a less stressful conclusion to the championship this weekend. He said the Mercedes driver has clearly proven himself a worthy champion.

“He’s winning a world championship and he’s going to win the world championship,” said Norris. “I don’t think anyone really cares how you do it honestly, they shouldn’t.

“He has done an incredible job and I would say he has done it in a pretty incredible way. People are saying he hasn’t had any tough competition this year but that proves exactly the point that he has done such an incredible a job.

“He’s got a very, very talented team mate that he’s beaten through the whole season. So I have nothing but respect for Kimi and he’s a very, very nice guy. We get along very well and I’m more than happy to pass the number one over to him. He deserves it.

“He’s done an incredible job, especially in his second year in Formula 1, to be the youngest world champion, all of these things that he’s going to achieve, that’s pretty insane. So I’m more than, happy, I enjoy seeing other people have that kind of success, so it’s nice to see.”

Norris scored back-to-back wins in the middle of the season and nearly scored another victory in Madrid where he lost the lead due to the timing of a Virtual Safety Car period. However McLaren’s form has slumped noticeably in recent races and they have fallen to fourth place in the constructors’ championship.

“I know I’ve had a pretty horrible defensive title, but there’s not much more I could have done,” he said. “I feel like I’ve driven a very, very good season.

“But I’m more than happy to pass the number one over to him because he deserves it easily more than anyone.”

Sports.title: Ducking Yoenli Hernandez Was Bentley’s Smartest Business Decision
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley no longer owns the WBO middleweight belt, but picking Shane Mosley Jr. over Yoenli Hernandez makes total sense for his career. Getting stripped of a world title is never an ideal situation.

Still, surrendering the hardware outside the ring sure beats taking a beating inside it against Hernandez. Bentley was simply not going to beat that guy.

By ducking Hernandez and sacrificing the WBO title, Bentley walks into an immediately winnable booking against Mosley Jr. instead. Dan Rafael reported that the WBO Grievance Committee officially dismissed Bentley’s appeal on Friday in a massive twenty-eight-page resolution. His November 7 bout can still proceed, yet he will enter the arena without his championship.

Dropping the belt hurts his prestige, but sharing twelve rounds with Hernandez would have extracted a much steeper toll. The Cuban amateur star operates as the real power at 160 pounds right now. Stepping into that mandatory test right as his promotional tenure began would have been sheer recklessness, especially with Hernandez likely stopping him early.

Mosley Jr. gives Bentley the perfect opening platform to look good under his new banner. Nobody should treat Mosley as a complete walkover, but that pairing remains manageable compared to facing the most lethal threat in the entire division.

The real prize sits just over the horizon. Should Bentley take care of business against Mosley, he immediately positions himself for massive in-house unification opportunities. Zuffa Boxing controls both IBF champion Aaron McKenna and WBC titlist Carlos Adames. A single victory over Mosley puts Bentley in prime position to challenge McKenna or Adames for their titles, completely bypassing the Cuban buzzsaw while fighting for even bigger gold.

Hernandez gets what he deserved anyway with an unblocked route to the vacant WBO strap. For Bentley, giving up the belt preserves his market value, protects his health, and sets up a direct line to brand-new world titles down the road.

Sports.title: Will Christian Mbilli Send Canelo Into Retirement?
Sports.content:
The former two-time undisputed super-middleweight world champion Saul “Canelo” Alvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) is a legend and a future Hall of Famer, but on Saturday night, October 31st, will the WBC champion Christian Mbilli send Canelo into retirement?

This world title bout is an intriguing matchup because it features Canelo’s skill set versus Mbilli’s work rate. The action is set to take place at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, airing live on DAZN PPV.

Back in June 2025, Christian Mbilli stopped Maciej Sulecki in the first round and won the WBC title. Three months later, Mbilli was involved in a hard-fought battle as his bout against Lester Martinez resulted in a split draw.

Going into this fight, the defending champion Christian Mbilli is the underdog. Despite the odds being against him, Mbilli has the opportunity to defeat the great Canelo Alvarez and send him into retirement.

Losing a fight is rare, but it’s not new to Canelo. What would be new is for him to lose this upcoming bout because it will mark the first time Canelo ever suffered back-to-back losses.

Suffering consecutive defeats could push Alvarez towards retirement. It’s a bold statement, and due to the statement, one would ask: what is Christian Mbilli’s path to victory?

Christian Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) is a determined, physical, and hungry world champion. He’s facing a tall task, but his path to victory is his aggression and his punch volume.

The 31-year-old Mbilli has incredible endurance, which allows him to constantly press forward and attack the body and head of his opponent. Alvarez has experienced stamina issues in the past, so outworking and outlasting Alvarez is Mbilli’s clear path to victory.

On the flip side, if the 36-year-old Canelo Alvarez has anything left in the tank, then this bout could be tailor-made for him due to the fact that Mbilli will be standing right in front of him.

In the past, Alvarez has done really well against opponents who lack movement and footwork. With Mbilli posting up in a neutral position and constantly in attack mode, Canelo will have many counterpunching opportunities.

Canelo will have his chances in regards to landing the left hook, the uppercut, and shots to the body. Speaking of body punches, those types of shots are a big part of Mbilli’s arsenal, and it will be interesting to see if he can consistently land shots to Canelo’s body.

Styles make fights, and that’s why the Canelo vs Mbilli fight will be an action-packed event. However, the question is, on Halloween night, will Canelo be sent into retirement, or will he take a step towards one last run at becoming undisputed once again?

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Must Demolish Inexperienced Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia cannot just settle for a win on Saturday; he needs to dominate. His opponent, Nikita Zon, has never boxed past eight rounds, yet finds himself stepping into a full twelve-round battle for the WBA super middleweight title in Riyadh.

On the scales, they matched up evenly, with Munguia clocking in at 167.4 pounds to Zon’s 167.5, but championship pedigree sets them worlds apart.

Zon brings an undefeated record, yet staying unblemished against modest competition is completely different from surviving world-class firepower. He stepped onto the stage looking like a man who knows exactly what he signed up for and wishes he hadn’t. That dead-eyed, heavy-footed demeanor on the scales says everything about where his head is at.

“This is his first scheduled twelve-round fight. Only fought three scheduled ten-round fights. Never fought longer than eight rounds,” Chris Mannix said on DAZN’s weigh-in broadcast. “Looks the part. Big, tall guy at 168 pounds. But this is a big, big challenge for Zon against Munguia.”

Those missing rounds matter when the fight goes deep. Zon will have to find out how his stamina holds up while taking heavy punishment from someone who practically lives in championship rounds. Looking cut on the scale does nothing to prove you can survive that furnace.

That puts the pressure squarely on Munguia to deliver a statement. He owns every edge needed to punish Zon to the body, test his gas tank early, and drag him into uncharted waters. Giving the challenger room to breathe would simply waste the advantages built up over years at the elite level.

There was plenty of talk about Munguia using extra footwork in his last outing, but staying on his toes against an overmatched opponent is not what fans want to see. Zon could theoretically shock everyone if he raises his game under pressure, since unbeaten fighters sometimes tap into another gear when everything is on the line. Still, a clean record cannot replace the stamina built from real championship rounds.

Munguia owns the title, the resume, and the edge. Now he just has to go out there and prove it. If he is serious about staying relevant at the absolute top of 168 pounds, he cannot mess around and box cute. He needs to walk Zon down and get him out of there fast.

With Munguia, there’s no such thing as a sure-thing win. We saw that in 2024 when he was knocked out by unknown Bruno Surace. That Surace disaster exposed the fatal flaw in treating any world-level booking as an easy night. Munguia walked into that ring looking right past an unheralded opponent, forgot his defense entirely, and paid for it by getting stretched out cold.

When a frontrunner fights down to the level of his competition or assumes a showcase win is guaranteed, disaster is always waiting. Zon is practically built in the exact same mold: obscure, fighting outside his home turf, possessing zero marquee names on his record, but completely free from the weight of expectations. All the pressure sits squarely on Munguia.

If he fights lazy, gets reckless, or leaves his chin hanging out like he did against Surace, even an inexperienced challenger can land the one punch that completely derails his career.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Gives Floyd Mayweather February 6 Ultimatum
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia wants Floyd Mayweather to stop talking and commit to February 6, but the bigger sales job is convincing fans that beating the retired star would carry championship value. Mayweather’s name can sell the event. His unbeaten record gives Garcia something even easier to advertise.

Garcia says Mayweather called him about the fight, and he is now demanding action. His latest post presents February 6 as a date he intends to keep, whether Floyd takes the offer or another opponent gets it.

“You called me and wanted this fight and I agree this is a big fight. But I am fighting FEB6th regardless so unless you actually make this happen then this fight is gone,” Garcia said on X. “You can go fight whoever but this is for a championship. I will TAKE you 0 with pleasure. Final warning no more games let’s make it happen.”

That unbeaten record is the prize Garcia keeps pointing toward. Taking Mayweather’s first professional defeat would generate enormous attention, but it would not mean Garcia had beaten the fighter who once ruled the sport. Floyd would enter February 6 at 49, approaching his 50th birthday.

Garcia is entitled to chase the biggest commercial fight available. Fans are equally entitled to distinguish between beating a famous former champion and beating an elite opponent in his prime. Putting a championship belt into the promotion does not erase that distinction.

Teofimo Lopez has also been mentioned for Garcia’s February return, giving this public ultimatum another purpose: pressure on Mayweather to commit while Garcia advertises that he has alternatives. February 6, 2027, was already being discussed before this latest post.

Ryan’s message establishes what he wants, rather than what both sides have signed. There is no completed agreement announced in the post, and his account of Mayweather’s call remains his account.

The demand is clear enough. Garcia wants Floyd’s name and unbeaten record on the contract. Until that happens, threatening to take the zero is promotion for a fight still waiting to become real.

It looks bad no matter how you view it. A prime fighter holding a major belt trying to strong-arm a fifty-year-old pensioner with a fake deadline is embarrassing theater. Giving Mayweather an ultimatum, as if Ryan is the A-side dictating terms to an icon old enough to be his father, makes Garcia look ridiculous rather than intimidating.

The optics are awful on every level. Floyd has not taken a genuine professional punch since Barack Obama was in the White House. His last legitimate pro test was an already-diminished Pacquiao over a decade ago, and his official retirement bout was a glorified sparring session against a debuting MMA fighter. Everything since has been low-effort exhibitions against kickboxers, reality stars, and YouTubers where nobody gets hurt.

Now you have Ryan, sitting in his physical prime, strutting around like he is doing the boxing world a favor by offering to beat up an inactive senior citizen. Demanding that Floyd hurry up and sign before February 6 only proves Ryan is desperate for the biggest possible check with the lowest possible threat level.

If Ryan really wanted to act like a world champion, he would be issuing ultimatums to Teofimo Lopez, Jaron Ennis, or the killer sharks at 140 and 147. Instead, he is publicly hounding a retired hall of famer to step into the ring so he can cosplay as the guy who conquered Mayweather’s record. Fans see right through it, and issuing a countdown clock to a grandfather only underlines how paper-thin the bravado is.

Sports.title: Oleksander Usyk Weight Cut Excuse Ready For Benavidez Bout
Sports.content:
David Benavidez spent years chasing Canelo Alvarez without ever landing the opportunity. Oleksandr Usyk could hand him the defining blockbuster that eluded him. Usyk takes on the physical risk, stepping down to 200 pounds after a long reign at heavyweight to face a younger, relentless pressure fighter built to break down tired opponents.

Usyk wants a return to cruiserweight for his next outing to target Benavidez, according to advisor Serhii Lapin speaking to Mike Coppinger of The Ring. Benavidez must handle business first against Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona, with three cruiserweight belts on the line. The potential clash with Usyk remains an ambitious goal instead of a signed deal.

The appeal for Benavidez stretches far past picking up more hardware. Taking down Usyk offers massive historical prestige, plus the distinct advantage of meeting him at cruiserweight instead of stepping up into heavyweight territory.

Usyk deserves credit for entertaining the idea. Past brilliance at 200 pounds offers no guarantee that his body responds well to another cut. He sits at 39 and turns 40 in January. Dropping weight after so long at heavyweight brings real volatility that glossy promotional hype easily ignores.

In top condition, Usyk possesses the foot speed and angles to keep Benavidez resetting, off balance, unable to plant his feet for heavy combinations. A sharp Usyk can disrupt incoming fire, spin his man, reset the pocket.

Trouble starts if cutting weight robs Usyk of his legs or tank. Benavidez thrives on grinding opponents down, making every exchange costly with dedicated work to the body through the championship rounds. Nobody can call Usyk depleted right now, but assuming the cut goes smoothly is just as reckless.

The built-in weight excuse angle is hard to ignore for Usyk, especially in modern boxing where fighters guard their reputations with an iron fist.

If Usyk drags Benavidez up to heavyweight and gets caught, battered, or outworked by a younger man, there is no safety net. He would lose as a heavyweight champion in his own division, full stop. By dropping to cruiserweight, his camp instantly constructs a built-in narrative cushion: he is almost 40 years old, he gave up size, he sacrificed his body to squeeze back down to 200 pounds for the fans, and he was depleted.

If he wins, he looks like an immortal wizard who conquered two divisions back and forth. If he loses, the media immediately frames it around the brutal weight cut rather than Benavidez simply beating him.

The physical reality makes the cruiserweight decision even more absurd. Benavidez has spent his entire career boiling down from heavyweight proportions. He rehydrated into the 180s and 190s just to bully super middleweights, and at cruiserweight he walks around comfortably above 215. Usyk weighed in the mid-220s for his heavyweight fights.

There is zero reason this fight could not happen at heavyweight, or at least a sensible catchweight, other than the tactical gamesmanship of the narrative.

Benavidez also plays along because he wants no part of heavyweights right now. Facing Usyk at 200 gives Benavidez the biggest brand name in the sport without having to step into the heavyweight ring against giant punchers. It lets Benavidez bypass the true divisional ruler, Jai Opetaia, avoid the terrifying risk of prime cruiserweights, and cash in against a depleted legend.

Both camps know exactly what they are doing. It provides Benavidez a shortcut to a massive scalp and gives Usyk a pre-packaged alibi if his legs fail him down the stretch.

Jai Opetaia belongs in this conversation too. The Ring previously reported Benavidez might target their cruiserweight champion after Cieslak. Moving toward Usyk creates a massive spectacle, yet it sidelines the most dangerous active force currently ruling the division.

Toppling Usyk creates an incredible legacy moment. It still leaves questions about true cruiserweight supremacy if Opetaia stays undefeated on the sideline.

Benavidez gets a crack at an all-time great. Usyk wagers his body can handle the scales without losing the stamina needed to survive deep water. That specific tension turns this matchup into must-see theater.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Looks Shaken At Weigh-In: Body Language Betrays Former King
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli plans on doing far more than just hanging onto his WBC super middleweight title against Canelo Alvarez in Riyadh. He claims he intends to beat the former champion at his own game, a risky declaration against a technician who thrives on catching aggressive punchers reckless enough to leave gaps.

Canelo answered at Friday’s weigh-in by pointing directly to his 21 years in the ring. The clash boils down to a classic style collision: Mbilli trying to swamp the veteran with sheer volume versus Canelo using veteran ring savvy to time incoming attacks.

That was not the swaggering, unflappable Canelo who used to smirk on the scales and mentally dismiss opponents before the opening bell even sounded.

The body language told the real story. When a fighter has to constantly recite their resume like a rehearsed script, it usually means they are trying to convince themselves just as much as the crowd. Canelo repeating that he has been doing this for 21 years sounded less like an intimidating warning and more like a fighter clinging to past glory to mask present doubt.

The physical reality is staring him right in the face. Canelo knows his gas tank is not what it used to be; his punch output drops every year, and resting on the ropes against a relentless engine like Mbilli is asking for trouble.

Mbilli throws punches in bunches, does not care about reputation, and attacks the midsection with bad intentions. Canelo looked like a veteran who fully realizes he signed up for an absolute grueling night at the office, where his mind might know the right counters to throw, but his legs and reflexes might not respond in time.

“You’re going to see on Saturday what’s going to happen. Tomorrow night, I’m going to beat him in every way. The better the technique, the better the punch. It will change my life a lot. After the victory, my life will change more. Fight of the year, an amazing fight. It will be incredible,” Mbilli stated at the scales.

A victory over Canelo brings instant worldwide credibility that owning a belt by itself never secures. Still, trying to prove he can outbox the Mexican star inside the pocket invites trouble. Mbilli operates best when crowding opponents, digging to the ribs, and forcing a relentless pace that drains older legs.

“This is very important for me. I’ve been doing this for 21 years. It’s important for me to take this title. Well, my experience is obviously very different. He’s never fought anyone like me. Tomorrow, he’s going to fight me,” Canelo said.

Ring mileage only works if Canelo makes Mbilli second-guess his charges. Sharp counterpunches can blunt the champion’s momentum and carve out breathing room between exchanges. Should Mbilli walk through those shots without blinking, ring wisdom alone will not generate the work rate needed to capture rounds on the cards.

Both men made weight without incident. Canelo tipped the scales at 167½ pounds, while Mbilli checked in at 167¾.

If Canelo cannot hurt Mbilli in the first four rounds and force him into retreat, he is in for a miserable evening trying to survive a non-stop wave of pressure.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Crawls Back To Bob Arum After Zuffa Disaster
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson catching up with Bob Arum feels like a smart play on familiar ground. Walking the free agent path lets him call his own shots, yet he still requires deep pockets to bankroll his ring returns plus a broadcaster ready to air them. Sitting idle for nearly twelve months makes those requirements impossible to brush aside.

Stevenson posted a picture flashing a wide grin next to his former promoter out in Houston. Coming off a quiet stint with Zuffa Boxing that failed to deliver an actual ring appearance, seeing Arum in person beats trading insults online over his market value.

🥊‼️Shakur Stevenson meeting with Bob Arum who has Raymond Muratalla the WBO MANDATORY on his stable‼️😳 https://t.co/Y7IRu55hBC — Hassan (@Hassanwellss) October 30, 2026

What Arum will do is facilitate business that serves Top Rank. The WBO ordering Shakur to face Raymond Muratalla at 140 pounds handed Arum all the cards. Muratalla is Top Rank’s guy. Arum can either negotiate a single-fight arrangement to put Shakur on a Top Rank card or push the bout to a purse bid, daring Shakur to find outside financiers willing to outbid ESPN’s ecosystem.

A permanent reunion will happen only if Shakur accepts a massive haircut on his financial expectations. If he still insists on purses detached from gate receipts and pay-per-view buys, Arum will simply use him for the Muratalla mandatory and let him drift back into the market to test reality all over again.

Arum bringing him back under a full, multi-fight promotional banner is another story entirely. Bob knows Shakur’s ceiling down to the exact dollar. Top Rank famously offered him a five-fight deal worth roughly $3 million a bout before he walked away, an offer Shakur rejected because he fancied himself a bona fide pay-per-view attraction. Arum will not bid against himself, nor will he overpay for a style that struggles to move tickets or drive commercial subscriptions.

What matters now is an official fight confirmation. Stevenson has spent enough time arguing about his worth from the sidelines. Whether Arum signs on for the long haul or just finances one night, sitting down together might finally get him back under the arena lights.

For the fighter, the upside makes total sense. Steering his own promotional ship grants creative freedom, but it leaves him hunting for funding, television clearance, plus opponents willing to accept realistic paydays. Total freedom never guarantees an actual fight night on its own.

Arum understands Stevenson’s talent inside the ropes, having spent years selling his headline slots. At the same time, he knows the financial ceiling. If Shakur continues demanding the massive purses reserved for pay-per-view draws, lunch together will not magically fix that gap.

Still, that photo blows up the narrative that Stevenson ran off every ally in boxing. Arum traveled to check in on him, and Shakur made sure the entire sport took notice.

Shakur found out the hard way that self-promotion requires somebody willing to write the check. He rode the wave on Turki Alalshikh cards against Zepeda and Teofimo Lopez, banking huge paydays while assuming that level of funding was the new industry baseline. Then came the Zuffa Boxing detour.

Dana White and company quickly realized what others already knew: paying an artist who fights safety-first eight figures while waiting out catchweight demands makes zero business sense. Zuffa cut their losses, showing him the door without staging a single fight.

Sitting inactive since January with zero broadcast platform and asking for money nobody wants to guarantee leaves him backed into a corner. That Houston photo with Arum was pure PR damage control. Shakur desperately needs the public to believe he has suitors, options, and warmth from the old guard, rather than looking like an isolated fighter out on an island.

Sports.title: Pointless Warburton Clash Wastes What Little Time Carlos Adames Has Left
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames begins his Zuffa Boxing journey with a matchup tailored to set up future UK bouts rather than create instant box office excitement. Ring Magazine officially confirmed that the WBC middleweight champion will meet Gerome Warburton on November 14, headlining Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13 in Saudi Arabia.

This non-title contest takes place above the middleweight limit. Former bantamweight champion Jason Moloney meets Andres Teran on the undercard. News of the matchup leaked on October 19, so today’s press release simply rubber stamps what everyone already knew.

Adames (25-1-1, 18 KOs) gets his chance to make an impression with his new promoter. Building real buzz with Warburton in the opposite corner remains a tough sell. The Welsh fighter sits at number seven in the WBA middleweight rankings, though that ranking looks better on paper than it resonates with mainstream fight fans.

Warburton (18-2-2 KOs) comes into the fight with back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney. Those victories opened the door for this spot, yet Adames marks a massive upgrade in difficulty. With only two knockouts on Warburton’s entire resume, the promotion cannot rely on a knockout artist angle.

The real motive here seems clear. Zuffa wants to prep Adames for bouts against stablemates Denzel Bentley and Aaron McKenna. Warburton serves as the first British obstacle before Zuffa rolls out bigger names from across the pond. While neither matchup is official, the blueprint makes sense.

Zuffa already has these fighters under contract. Adames gives Bentley and McKenna a legitimate champion to target. A dominant showing against Warburton hands the promotional team fresh footage to roll out for the next phase.

Still, convincing audiences to tune in for the current plan is a different story. Bentley and McKenna give British spectators a hometown reason to care, but domestic ties do not guarantee a massive gate or monster television ratings. In the United States, neither matchup feels like a breakout attraction for Adames.

Bentley’s status complicates things even further. He risks losing his WBO belt after failing to secure a date with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez. Strip away that belt, and an Adames clash loses much of its luster.

McKenna presents another route, yet the middleweight division continues struggling with star power. Matching in-house talent creates reliable action, but it rarely draws casual viewers into the weight class.

This is classic in-house recycling that completely ignores both the clock on Adames’ career and what actual ticket-buying fight fans care about.

Adames is 32, fights roughly once a year, and carries zero commercial crossover. Handing him Gerome Warburton in a non-title catchweight does nothing. It does not sell tickets, it does not draw eyes to a broadcast, and it certainly does not move the needle for casual viewers who have never heard of the guy. Fans know a glorified sparring session when they see one, so they simply tune out.

The logic of using Warburton as a stepping stone to Denzel Bentley or Aaron McKenna is just as flawed. That entire sequence assumes the public is clamoring to see Adames clean out the British domestic scene. They are not. Bentley and McKenna are solid operators, but neither is a global draw capable of transforming Adames into an attraction.

If the payoff at the end of the tunnel is lukewarm to begin with, burning four to six months on a preliminary warm-up against Warburton makes zero promotional sense.

Time is working against them. With his history of lengthy layoffs, Adames cannot afford to spend prime months ticking boxes for low-profile regional setups. If Zuffa wanted to make a real statement with their middleweight investment, going after recognized names like Tim Tszyu or Vito Mielnicki Jr. would have delivered immediate legitimacy.

Putting Adames in with names fans actually follow forces attention onto the division, creates genuine stakes, and gives Zuffa an immediate return on their money.

Instead, they went the safe, budget-conscious route. The problem is that safety breeds indifference. When the opening move fails to capture anyone’s imagination, the matches lined up behind it end up dead on arrival anyway.

Ghana News.title: We believe 5G investment underscores our commitment to sustaining network quality, supporting Ghana’s growing digital connectivity – MTN
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana says it is currently finalising the required formalities and payment obligations associated with the acquisition of a 5G license.

According to the telecom giant, the US$202 million spectrum acquisition cost is already reflected in its free cash flow outlook.

Therefore, the payment for the license acquisition does not change its 2026 free cash flow and dividend outlook.

“We believe this investment underscores our commitment to sustaining network quality and building the capacity required to support Ghana’s growing digital connectivity needs”, it disclosed in its quarter 3 2026 financial report.

During quarter 3, MTN achieved a significant milestone with the notification from the National Communications Authority (NCA) of the award of spectrum in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands for 5G and mobile broadband services. The award comprises 2x20 MHz in the 700 MHz band and 1x150 MHz in the 3 GHz band, with licenses valid for 15 years.

MTN said the additional spectrum will complement its existing spectrum assets and strengthen

its ability to meet growing demand for high-speed connectivity and data-centric services across Ghana.

“Following the issuance of the licenses, we will deploy the newly awarded spectrum to support the rollout of 5G services, enhance service quality and customer experience as data usage grows, and further strengthen our network capabilities. The additional capacity will also strengthen our Home broadband proposition, allowing us to extend high-speed connectivity to more households and broaden our addressable home market”, it added.

MTN concluded by appreciating the continued support of its shareholders, regulators and other stakeholders as it undertakes this important investment in Ghana’s telecommunications infrastructure.

Ghana News.title: Youth unemployment exceeds 32%; about 12m Ghanaians are between 15 and 35 years – GSS
Ghana News.content:
About 12 million Ghanaians were aged 15 to 35 in 2025, roughly one in every three people and the largest youth population in the country’s history.

The figures are presented in Ghana in Numbers, 2025, the new annual flagship publication of the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS), which brings official statistics on Ghana’s population, economy, society, governance and environment into one accessible volume.

The report examines whether Ghana’s large youth population is being matched by the education, skills and work opportunities needed for young people to participate fully in the economy.

Youth unemployment remains above the national rate

During the first three quarters of 2025, unemployment averaged 32.4% among people aged 15 to 24 and 21.9% among those aged 15 to 35. The national average was 12.8 percent.

This means that young jobseekers were more likely than the wider labour force to be unable to find work.

The average rate of young people aged 15 to 35 who were neither employed nor enrolled in education or training (known as the NEET rate) was 17.9% during the first three quarters of 2025.

In the third quarter alone, close to two million people aged 15 to 35 were in this group. Women made up more than 60%. The rate was 20.6% in urban areas, 18.0% in rural areas and 25.3% in the Central Region.

Job quality and skills matching also matter

About 65% of employed youth said their skills fitted their jobs, but only 58% said their level of education matched what the job required.

More than 70.0% of all jobs were informal. This means that the youth employment question is not only whether a person works, but also whether the work uses the person’s training and provides stable, protected employment.

Dr. Alhassan Iddrisu, Government Statistician, said the labour figures should be read together: “Close to two million young people are neither working nor in education or training, what we refer to as the NEET group, and more than six in ten of them are young women.”

Ghana’s demographic opportunity is time-bound

The share of children aged 0 to 14 fell from 41.8% of the population in 2000 to 35.0% in 2025, while the youth share remained at about 35%. Ghana now has roughly as many people aged 15 to 35 as children aged 0 to 14.

This age structure can support faster development when a larger working-age population has the health, skills and jobs to be productive. The report says Ghana’s demographic window opened in the early 2000s and has been narrowing since 2019.

“Ghana’s youth window is open, but it is closing,” Dr. Iddrisu said. “Our choices on schooling, skills and jobs in the next ten years will decide whether it becomes a dividend or a burden.”

Evidence for education, employment and skills planning

Ghana in Numbers, 2025 brings population, labour market, education and skills indicators together to support decisions that can be tracked over time. Future editions will monitor youth unemployment, the NEET rate, informal work and the match between schooling and jobs.

The publication and related data resources are available through the Ghana Statistical Service website, StatsBank and the GSS Stats App.

Ghana News.title: The cost of staying alive: diabetes, hypertension and the price of a working life in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
As diabetes and hypertension threaten the health, livelihoods and productivity of working-age Ghanaians, two personal stories reveal the human cost of chronic illness and the urgent need for early detection, accessible treatment and supportive workplaces.

At an age when many young people are building careers, raising families and pursuing their ambitions, others are confronting illnesses that threaten their health and financial security. For some, a chronic disease diagnosis becomes more than a medical challenge; it becomes a struggle to remain employed, afford treatment and plan for the future.

Trudy Nartey, 45, knows this reality. Diagnosed with diabetes in her twenties, she has experienced how a condition requiring continuing care can reshape a person's working life.

She previously worked at a private company, where she frequently requested permission to attend medical appointments and receive treatment. According to her account, her employment was eventually terminated because of these repeated requests.

She remained unemployed for almost two years, struggling to afford her medication, before eventually securing employment in the government sector.

Her experience exposes a difficult intersection between healthcare and economic security. When income disappears, the need for medication does not. For workers with chronic conditions, employment can mean more than a monthly salary; it can determine whether continuing treatment remains affordable.

For Kwesi Yeboah Nketiah, 31, the discovery of hypertension came through a frightening medical emergency.

He felt dizzy and collapsed before being rushed to hospital, where he was admitted for several days while his blood pressure was managed. He was diagnosed with hypertension during that admission. Kwesi now takes his medication regularly, although he sometimes worries about having to take drugs throughout his life.

His concern reflects the psychological adjustment that can follow a chronic disease diagnosis, particularly among younger people who may not have anticipated years of treatment.

A growing national concern

The World Health Organisation (WHO) reported that the number of people living with diabetes worldwide rose from 200 million in 1990 to 830 million in 2022. In 2022, approximately 14 per cent of adults aged 18 and older had diabetes.

Hypertension is equally concerning. The WHO estimated that 1.4 billion adults aged 30 to 79 were living with the condition in 2024. Around 44 per cent were unaware they had it, while only about 23 per cent had their blood pressure under control.

Ghana's figures reinforce the urgency. The 2023 WHO STEPwise Approach to Noncommunicable Disease Risk Factor Surveillance (STEPS) survey found that 21.7 per cent of adults aged 18 to 69 had hypertension, while 5.2 per cent had raised blood glucose. More than half of adults with elevated blood pressure had not previously been diagnosed.

Meanwhile, figures from Ghana's Ministry of Health, reported by Graphic Online in September 2026, showed 577,374 recorded hypertension cases in 2025, down slightly from 583,720 in 2024. These are reported cases, not a count of everyone living with the condition.

The figures underline the importance of screening. Hypertension can remain undetected because it often causes no obvious symptoms, while elevated blood glucose may also go unnoticed without appropriate testing.

The kidney connection

Reacting to the issue Dr Abdul Wahab Agbeve, Director of Agbeve Hospital at Sowutuom, a suburb of Accra, warned that diabetes and hypertension can undermine workplace productivity, increase healthcare expenditure and impose financial and psychological burdens on patients and their families.

He explained that one of the major health concerns associated with the two conditions is their potential to damage the kidneys. Diabetes can harm the small blood vessels responsible for filtering waste from the blood, while prolonged, uncontrolled hypertension can damage kidney blood vessels and impair their function.

Dr Agbeve noted that, over time, these changes may lead to chronic kidney disease and, in severe cases, kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplantation.

He highlighted the financial and occupational implications of these complications, pointing out that frequent hospital visits, specialist treatment and dialysis can consume time and income, disrupt employment and place considerable pressure on household finances.

According to Dr Agbeve, kidney disease may also progress without obvious symptoms in its early stages, making regular medical monitoring particularly important for people living with diabetes or hypertension.

He emphasised that these complications are not inevitable, explaining that early diagnosis, appropriate treatment and regular medical follow-up can help reduce the risks, although outcomes vary from person to person.

When illness affects productivity

The economic consequences of diabetes and hypertension extend beyond hospital bills. Medical appointments, periods of illness and hospital admissions can interrupt work schedules, while serious complications may affect a person's ability to perform usual duties.

Employers may face staffing pressures and additional costs. Workers, meanwhile, may worry about lost earnings, job security and the long-term affordability of treatment.

Yet chronic illness does not automatically make someone an unproductive employee. With appropriate care and reasonable workplace support, many people living with diabetes or hypertension continue to work effectively.

Trudy’s experience highlights the difficulties that can arise when employment arrangements do not accommodate continuing healthcare needs. Kwesi's concerns demonstrate that managing chronic illness also involves emotional adjustment, not merely taking medication.

Dr Agbeve's observations highlight the importance of addressing these conditions early, before complications become severe enough to affect a person's ability to work and maintain financial independence.

For employees, access to medical care and the flexibility to attend appointments can make a significant difference in managing chronic conditions. For employers, supportive workplace policies can help retain experienced workers while reducing avoidable disruptions associated with poorly managed illnesses.

Prevention and shared responsibility

Dr Agbeve emphasised the importance of healthier dietary habits, public awareness and appropriate medical care in reducing the burden of diabetes and hypertension.

Eating a balanced diet, consuming more vegetables, limiting sugary drinks, reducing excessive salt intake and engaging in regular physical activity can help lower certain health risks. However, lifestyle changes cannot prevent every case and must not replace prescribed treatment.

Regular blood pressure checks, appropriate blood glucose testing and kidney assessments when recommended can help identify health problems and guide care. People diagnosed with chronic conditions should follow their healthcare professionals' advice and consult them before changing medication.

Dr Agbeve stressed that early detection and appropriate management are important in reducing the risk of complications, including kidney damage, and supporting better long-term health outcomes.

Employers also have a role to play. Establishing fair arrangements for medical appointments and leave can help workers manage their health without unnecessarily jeopardising their livelihoods.

Healthcare providers, policymakers and employers must therefore recognise that managing chronic diseases involves more than prescribing medication. It also requires accessible healthcare services, public education, regular monitoring and working environments that allow people to manage their conditions responsibly.

Trudy's return to employment and Kwesi's commitment to treatment reveal the importance of looking beyond diagnosis to the circumstances in which people live and work. For Ghana, tackling diabetes and hypertension is not simply a health priority. It is an investment in protecting livelihoods, supporting families and sustaining national productivity.

Ghana News.title: Shoe-making is not for school dropouts — Horseman founder Tonyi Senayah
Ghana News.content:
Founder of Horseman, Tonyi Senayah, says his shoemaking business is driven by a broader mission to create fulfilling employment opportunities for artisans and challenge the perception that vocational trades are meant for people who fail to progress through formal education.

Mr Senayah said his interest in developing people, which took shape towards the end of his studies at the University of Ghana, had influenced his decision to build a business around shoemaking and craftsmanship.

Speaking on Personality Profile on JoyNews on Friday, October 30, he said that although he once dreamed of becoming a pilot, he had become increasingly drawn to work that would help people develop their potential.

As he approached the end of university, he said he knew he wanted to work in a field where he could contribute to human development. He subsequently applied to several international non-governmental organisations working in that area.

His eventual entry into entrepreneurship through shoemaking, he explained, remained consistent with that ambition.

“When the entrepreneurship started and it happened to be shoes, working with artisans, it wasn't so far off. It was still a calling to help shape and develop people, create opportunities for people who had learned the skill of shoemaking and craft in general,” he said.

Beyond making shoes

Mr Senayah said his experience working with artisans had drawn his attention to the circumstances under which many people entered vocational trades.

He observed that some people learnt shoemaking, sewing, mechanics and carpentry not necessarily because those were their preferred careers, but because they had been unable to continue their formal education.

According to him, that reality reinforced his determination to build a business that offered artisans more fulfilling employment opportunities while helping to change public attitudes towards vocational skills.

He said the ambition was not simply to provide work for people who had acquired practical skills but also to help them see greater value in their craft and in the contribution they could make to society.

Challenging the stigma

Mr Senayah said one of his broader objectives was to challenge the perception that vocational training was an option reserved for people who could not make it into secondary school or follow conventional academic paths.

He argued that the circumstances that led someone into a trade should not determine how society valued that person or the work they did.

His vision for Horseman, therefore, extends beyond producing shoes to creating opportunities for artisans and helping to shift attitudes towards technical and vocational occupations.

The founder said he wanted his work to demonstrate that people who had acquired practical skills could build fulfilling careers and contribute meaningfully to the economy.

For him, developing people and creating opportunities for skilled workers remain central to the purpose that shaped his journey into entrepreneurship.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana reports 44.4% growth in mobile money transactions as digital services expand
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana has reported a 44.4 per cent year-on-year increase in the value of Mobile Money transactions for the first half of 2026, alongside plans to invest US$1.1 billion over three years to expand its network infrastructure and digital services across the country.

The company disclosed this at a Regional Media and Stakeholder Engagement in the Volta Region, where management outlined its financial performance, network expansion plans and digital financial services.

MTN Ghana’s General Manager for Southern Ghana, David Gyimah Boadi, said the company had earmarked approximately US$380 million for investment in 2026 as part of the three-year programme.

He said the investment was intended to improve network capacity, service quality and infrastructure resilience amid growing demand for digital services.

As part of the expansion, MTN plans to deploy 500 new network sites across Ghana in 2026, with the Volta Region among the areas expected to benefit.

The company is also upgrading existing rural network infrastructure to extend 4G connectivity to underserved communities.

The Senior Manager for Sales in the South East, Princess Owusu Nyarko, said the expansion involved identifying communities with coverage gaps, constructing new sites and upgrading existing infrastructure to improve service delivery.

She said the company was also working with technology innovators and industry partners to prepare for emerging connectivity needs.

Financial performance

MTN Ghana also reported growth in its financial performance for the first half of 2026.

Service revenue reached GH¢15 billion, representing a 32.3 per cent increase, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose by 47.1 per cent to GH¢9.3 billion.

Profit after tax increased by 46.8 per cent to GH¢5.1 billion, according to figures presented by the company.

MTN further reported that Mobile Money transaction volumes and revenue each grew by 23.3 per cent during the period, while the number of active users increased by 3.1 per cent.

The company said it was strengthening security measures and customer education to address fraud risks associated with the growing use of digital financial services.

Support for businesses

On support for businesses, MTN Ghana’s Network Manager for the South East, Duku Samuel, said the company was providing tailored products for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

These included specialised voice bundles, the SME bundle and JIMAPA, a package designed for women in business.

He said the company was also expanding fibre broadband services and digital payment solutions for businesses, households, enterprises and government agencies.

Investment in education and healthcare

Beyond telecommunications, MTN Ghana highlighted its investments in education, healthcare and digital skills development.

The company said the MTN Ghana Foundation commissioned and handed over an Accident and Emergency Centre valued at GH¢15.4 million to the Ho Teaching Hospital in March 2026.

It also reported that its Girls-in-ICT programme had trained 1,000 girls and 100 teachers in the Volta Region in basic information and communications technology (ICT), digital skills and work readiness, in collaboration with the Ministry of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovation.

Nationally, the company said its Skills Academy had equipped more than 100,000 young people with digital literacy, financial skills and career-readiness competencies.

Sustainability initiatives

MTN Ghana also outlined measures under its sustainability strategy, including the use of solar power at selected network sites, waste separation, recycling and responsible water management.

The company’s Media Relations Adviser, Shiela Sorinye, said sustainability had been integrated into its Ambition 2030 strategy, with measures aimed at reducing its environmental footprint.

The company also reported paying GH¢5.6 billion in direct and indirect taxes and GH¢384.7 million in fees and levies during the first half of 2026.

MTN Ghana, which is marking 30 years of operations in the country, said it would continue investing in network expansion, digital financial services, customer experience and business solutions as part of its growth strategy.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest woman, offer GH¢100,000 reward for Sakumono murder suspect
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 47-year-old woman in connection with the killing of two relatives at the NTHC Estate, Sakumono, in the Greater Accra Region, and declared the principal suspect wanted.

The suspect, identified as Beatrice Mumuni, is believed to have led Samuel Christopher Osei Anto to the residence of the deceased before the murders, according to a police statement

The victims, George Atuguba, 57, and his 47-year-old niece, Irene Atuguba, were killed on Friday, October 30, 2026.

The police have declared Osei Anto wanted to assist investigations and are offering a reward of GH¢100,000 for credible information leading to his arrest.

Police appeal for information

In a statement announcing the arrest, the police urged anyone with information about the whereabouts of Osei Anto to report to the nearest police station.

The public may also contact the police through the emergency numbers 191 or 18555.

The arrest follows preliminary police findings that the killings may have been triggered by a financial dispute involving George Atuguba, who allegedly owed GH¢500,000.

The police had earlier said Osei Anto reportedly went to the victims’ residence with Mumuni to demand repayment of the money, after which a misunderstanding allegedly occurred and the two victims were shot.

The circumstances surrounding the killings remain under investigation.

The police have appealed for public assistance as efforts continue to locate Osei Anto and establish the full circumstances of the incident.

Ghana News.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
Ghana News.content:
The US has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically-needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks, after Kyiv said deliveries had been delayed in recent months.

The US State Department said the advanced PAC-3 interceptor missiles would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn) and would be "funded entirely" by Kyiv's allies in Europe and Canada.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly urged the US to speed up deliveries of its Patriots - the only effective weapon in downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles.

The latest move comes just days after a row between Zelensky and Donald Trump, with the US president saying it was time for Ukraine to get a new leader to try to end the war with Russia.

In Friday's statement, the State Department said "this proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe".

It said "Ukraine will pay for this purchase with donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan".

The statement said the "principal contractor" would be American company Lockheed Martin, adding that "no US funds are involved in this sale".

Zelensky said earlier this week that his country had been waiting almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies.

And in a Telegram post late on Friday, the Ukrainian president reported that earlier in the day Russian ballistic missiles had struck two of the country's regions.

"They continue to carry out terrorist strikes against our cities," he said.

Zelensky has recently admitted that Ukraine was running critically low on Patriots, as Russia was intensifying its attacks on key energy infrastructure ahead of winter.

Kyiv desperately needs the interceptors but there is a global shortage of the munitions due to their use by the US in its war against Iran.

It is not clear what the production schedule will be for the Patriots - but it is understood the order is for new builds rather than existing missiles, meaning there is unlikely to be any kind of rapid delivery to Ukraine.

Patriots also have lengthy production times, with only 600 missiles produced per year according to the US Department of Defence.

Ghana News.title: Ghana and Burkina Faso seek stronger trade and industrial cooperation at SIAO 2026
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening trade and investment relations with Burkina Faso through a proposed bilateral trade agreement aimed at promoting industrial cooperation, cross-border trade and value addition.

The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, announced this during the opening ceremony of the 18th International Arts and Crafts Fair of Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026) on Friday, October 30.

Delivering the Guest of Honour address, she highlighted opportunities for the two countries to collaborate in handicrafts, agro-processing, shea, cotton, leather and agricultural value chains.

Ghana, which is participating as Guest of Honour alongside Mali and Niger, is showcasing products from all 16 regions at the fair.

The exhibition features a range of Ghanaian products, including Kente, Adinkra, fugu, Bolgatanga baskets, beads, pottery, leather goods and contemporary fashion.

Madam Ofosu-Adjare disclosed that formal trade between Ghana and Burkina Faso exceeded US$1 billion last year.

She stressed the need to strengthen border management, harmonise product standards and facilitate the movement of goods between the two countries to further expand trade.

The proposed bilateral agreement is expected to provide a framework for advancing cooperation and creating opportunities for businesses in both countries.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
