Claustro del monasterio de Santo Domingo, en Jaén. diego grandi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La conexión del poeta alicantino con Jaén se inició cuando fue destinado como comisario de Cultura para dirigir el periódico Altavoz del Frente Sur. Coincidiendo con el 84º aniversario de su muerte, la ciudad de Jaén estrenó una ruta literaria que recorre los lugares de su estancia en tierras jiennenses, desde la plaza de los Naranjos, bautizada también como plaza de Miguel Hernández, y que continúa por el refugio antiaéreo de la plaza de Santiago, donde se rememora el bombardeo de Jaén del 1 de abril de 1937 que se saldó con 159 muertos y decenas de heridos. Cuando el bombardeo de Jaén, Miguel Hernández se encontraba fuera cubriendo la batalla de Peñarroya o en la defensa de Medellín, pero Josefina Manresa sí que fue testigo directo.

El otro pilar clave fue su esposa, que era natural de Quesada, localidad que es la cuna del río Guadalquivir y donde desde el año 2015 hay un museo en memoria de los dos. Tras convertirse en la viuda de un poeta maldito, Josefina guardó celosamente los escritos de Miguel, como centinela de su memoria, para que nadie pudiera arrebatarle ese tesoro; documentos de su marido que durante años mantuvo escondidos en costales de los que se utilizaban para llenar el trigo. En el museo quesadeño, que comparte instalaciones con el dedicado al pintor Rafael Zabaleta, se hace un recorrido por la obra y la vida del poeta y su esposa, una historia de amor llena de pasiones y emociones. Como esta carta en la que ella relata sus primeros encuentros: “Me estuvo pretendiendo desde el año 1933 hasta el 27 de septiembre del 34. Pasaba varias veces por la puerta del taller de la calle Mayor, en Orihuela, donde yo trabajaba de modista. Miraba hacia dentro del taller y me di cuenta que me miraba a mí”.

Su estancia en Jaén fue la que inspiró otro de sus poemas más célebres, Aceituneros, que pone letra al himno de la provincia. La coral Encina Hermosa, de Castillo de Locubín, lo ha versionado ahora en clave feminista:

Andaluzas de Jaén

aceituneras comprometidas

decidme en el alma: ¿quién

recogió las olivas?

No las recogió la nada,

ni el dinero, ni el señor

sino la mujer arrastrada,

el cariño y el tesón

Conectada a la luna

y a la rociá de la mañana

las tres dieron la vida

a ese olivo y a sus ramas

Levántate aceitunera de plata

decimos al pie del viento

la aceitunera alzó su mano

poderosa de miramiento

Andaluzas de Jaén

aceituneras comprometidas

decidme en el alma: ¿quién

amamantó los olivos?

Nuestra sangre, nuestro cuerpo

no sólo la del hombre

que se llevó el mérito

de nuestro sufrimiento

Andaluzas, levantémonos

reclamemos nuestro lugar

La fachada de la fundación Miguel Hernández, en Orihuela, donde nació el poeta. mauritius images/ Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Siguiendo la Senda del Poeta

Ya en la provincia de Alicante, y con el río Segura como compañero de viaje, nos adentramos en la llamada Senda del Poeta creada por varias instituciones levantinas en homenaje al escritor, natural de Orihuela. Este itinerario, que puede realizarse en cualquier época del año, se efectúa a pie durante tres días desde la Casa Museo de Miguel Hernández en Orihuela hasta su tumba en el cementerio de Alicante.

Esta ruta, que atraviesa el sendero de gran recorrido GR-125, está dividida en tres etapas. Arranca en Orihuela, ciudad donde nació Miguel Hernández el 30 de octubre de 1910. Orihuela marcó su infancia y juventud de forma decisiva, ya que aquí fue donde inició sus estudios escolares en el colegio Santo Domingo, ayudó a su padre en los trabajos de pastoreo, participó en las reuniones literarias de la tahona de los hermanos Fenoll, publicó sus primeros poemas y conoció a Josefina Manresa. A continuación, se pasa por Redován, donde nació su progenitor, por Callosa del Segura, se llega a Cox, donde Hernández y Manresa vivieron varios años; por Elche, donde murieron su mujer e hijo, y concluye en Alicante.

La primera etapa transcurre también por Granja de Rocamora y finaliza en Albatera, en cuyo término se encontraba el campo de concentración donde perecieron muchos compañeros de Hernández tras la Guerra Civil. Todo ello por caminos con numerosos huertos de naranjos y limoneros que ofrecen al caminante el penetrante olor del azahar, característico de la primavera en la vega baja del río Segura.

La segunda etapa del sendero, entre caminos donde predominan las palmeras, transcurre entre Albatera y Elche, adonde se trasladó Josefina Manresa con su hijo Manuel Miguel tras la muerte del poeta. En el Archivo Municipal de Elche se encuentran depositados un buen número de manuscritos del poeta y aquí también se encuentra la Universidad pública Miguel Hernández que, en 1998, nombró al poeta Doctor Honoris Causa a título póstumo.

El palmeral de la ciudad de Elche, una de las paradas siguiendo las huellas de Miguel Hernández. José Antonio Aldeguer ( GETTY IMAGES )

Finalmente, la tercera y última etapa discurre entre Elche y Alicante, en cuya cárcel falleció el 28 de marzo de 1942. Aquí redactó sus últimos poemas de Cancionero y romancero de ausencias, y en las dependencias de la enfermería carcelaria contrajo matrimonio canónico con Josefina Manresa días antes de morir.

En el cementerio de Alicante, entre campos de almendros, reposan los restos del poeta en una tumba en donde también se encuentran enterrados su mujer y su hijo.

World.title: Fears spread over Gen Z riot plans across NL
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

There are fears that a “Gen Z” protest, inspired by the ongoing unrest that has swept through France and other countries, could hit the Netherlands over the weekend.

A report in AD found that groups on Telegram, Snapchat and other social media platforms are preparing to riot in cities including The Hague, Maastricht and Eindhoven.

While no applications for protest permits have been submitted, police have said they generally monitor online forums for signs of trouble but would not comment on this matter specifically.

The messages, which include calls to loot shopping centres, were enough to prompt school heads to issue warnings to parents in Maastricht. Limburg police backed the warnings, according to local broadcaster L1 News.

Shopkeepers in The Hague have also started boarding up their windows as a precaution, as some messaging groups are calling for gatherings on the Malieveld and attacks on commercial centres nearby, according to Omroep West.

The protests in France, which have spread to Italy and Spain began over education and living standards among young people. Many of the demonstrations quickly descended into serious rioting, often with heavy police response.

There are similar concerns in Germany, where youth groups are preparing to protest over similar issues on Halloween.

World.title: “No movement” in cabinet talks amid left-right stalemate
World.content:
The cabinet’s attempt to win over left- and right-wing opposition parties in its ongoing tax plan talks failed again on Friday.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and other senior ministers met opposition leaders a day after three right-wing parties, the far-right JA21, orthodox Protestant SGP and farmer-citizen movement BBB, banded together to push their demands as a single bloc. The demands range from harsher asylum measures and changes to abortion rules to scrapping a tax rise to pay for defence.

The move was the latest attempt by the opposition to force the cabinet to pick a side. Opposition parties have said for weeks that the cabinet will never get a broad agreement, because the two sides of the aisle have incompatible demands.

The offer presented on Friday covered how to pay for changes to box 3, the tax on savings and investments, without raising taxes on wealth, sources told the Telegraaf.

The cabinet would use money left over from a fund to refund people who were overtaxed under box 3 in past years, and cut taxes for business owners who pay themselves profits from their own companies. It would also keep a tax deduction for healthcare costs that was due to be scrapped in 2028.

Regardless of the offer, the stalemate appears to continue. Centre-left PRO leader Jesse Klaver said he saw “no movement at all” on his party’s demand for higher taxes on the wealthy and lower taxes on workers.

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans called it “a tough, complicated conversation”, but said the new right-wing alliance remained intact.

The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA does not have a majority, so it needs support from opposition parties to get its tax plan through parliament.

World.title: Government seeks to ban smoking where children congregate
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet wants to prohibit smoking at locations dominated by children, including petting zoos and after-school and other managed playgrounds.

Sources told broadcaster NOS the proposed ban will be discussed at Friday’s Council of Ministers.

While most such places are already smoke-free, the government wants to ensure that the remaining few ban smoking. The House of Representatives also supports the ban and wanted to extend it to other kid-friendly locations like zoos and amusement parks.

That may come in the future, along with bans at unattended playgrounds and outdoor swimming pools, but for now, the government will focus on managed playgrounds and day care centres where there is wide support for the plan.

The ban is part of the government’s efforts to have a smoke-free generation by 2040. Measures already in place include a display ban, unattractive packaging and fewer locations to purchase cigarettes.

World.title: Herman Brood painting added to national art collection
World.content:
A painting by rock legend and artist Herman Brood has been added to the National Collection, placing Brood in the company of Dutch icons such as Rembrandt, Ferdinand Bol, Piet Mondriaan and Karel Appel.

“We believe that Herman Brood should be given more prestige as an icon of the twentieth century as an artist,” said the cultural heritage anency (RCE).

The untitled acrylic work, made with an ever-present injection syringe and paint rollers, features two men with a pistol. It has been hanging on the wall of the tax office in The Hague but was moved earlier this week to the RCE’s depot in Amersfoort, where it’s been given the name “rock-‘n-roll on canvas”.

The inclusion of the work in the 120,000-strong national collection is official recognition that Brood has contributed substantially to Dutch culture and history. The work will be preserved permenantly and can be lent to museums.

“Junkie who painted”

Rob Dupré, a friend of “The Never Be Clever” and “Saturday Night” singer who died in 2001, told broadcaster NOS that Brood would rise from the dead if he heard the news.

“In life, he was seen as a rock ‘n’ roll singer who worked as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if everyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympics,” said Dupré, who works to detect counterfeits attributed to the artist.

It’s thought the painting ended up in the tax office to pay off a debt. “He didn’t do receipts and that kind of civil matter,” Dupré said. “He painted five paintings and then spent them on alcohol, drugs and women. He wasn’t really businesslike.”

As to the painting now part of the Rijks collection, Dupré says: “Have you ever had an envelope from the Tax and Customs Administration?… He deliberately painted those two people’s sweaters in exactly the same colour.”

As for the gun? “Everyone would want to have that in their hand when you get a tax assessment, right?” Dupré told AD.

Great honour

“He would have thought this was a great honour,” Brood’s wife Xandra Brood told the AD, adding that she had to point out colours to him because the artist was colour-blind. “He worked very fast and made several paintings one after the other.”

She hopes the painting will eventually hang on the walls of Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum, his greatest wish.

This painting’s estimated value is 13,000 to 15,000 euros, but Dupré says that’s maybe gone up 50% since the painting became part of the national collection Thursday.

That inclusion, says Dupré, is official recognition of the artist’s craftsmanship. “He was much more than a side-working rock star. And that is now being recognised.”

World.title: French customs seize thousands of THC sweets bound for NL
World.content:
French customs officers have intercepted 3,560 packs of cannabis-laced sweets that were being shipped from the US to the Netherlands, the European anti-fraud office OLAF said on Thursday.

The sweets contained THC, the main psychoactive substance in cannabis. Of the packs, 3,213 copied the look of a “very well-known European gummy brand”, using altered lettering to resemble its name. OLAF did not name the brand. All the packs have been destroyed.

OLAF did not say who the sweets were meant to be delivered to in the Netherlands.

In a statement, the agency said the familiar packaging gives the false impression of an ordinary, safe product, but that a single product could contain a high amount of THC, and children could be at risk.

Cannabis sweets have caused several scares in the Netherlands. This summer, Utrecht police warned parents after two children became ill from sweets found in a school playground, broadcaster NOS reported.

World.title: Seven Rotterdam police officers to face trial over arrest death
World.content:
Seven police officers will go on trial in January next year over the death of a 32-year-old man who was held in a “prone position” on the ground for a long time after being tasered during an arrest in Rotterdam in 2023, the public prosecution department (OM) said on Thursday.

Two officers chased the man on June 9 that year, first in a police van and then on foot, after reports that he had crashed his bicycle into a car and then cycled on.

When he ignored their instructions, one officer used a taser, but it did not incapacitate him or stop him from further resisting. More officers arrived and several of them pinned him down. Soon after he became unwell and was given CPR but died in hospital.

In February 2024 the OM said it would prosecute eight officers after an investigation by the Rijksrecherche, which investigates the police. A pathologist concluded the man’s death could have been caused by the way he was restrained.

The officers are accused of breaching the rules on the use of force with fatal consequences, which has been a criminal offence in its own right since July 2022.

The OM said on Thursday it had dropped a case against an eighth officer, as he was still in training and was following instructions.

The case will be heard on January 19 and from February 15 to 18 by the Blauwe Kamer, a special court in Utrecht that handles cases against police officers. The court will rule on all seven cases at the same time.

In September another Rotterdam man, Alfredo Goeloe (51), died during an arrest after collapsing while officers held him on the ground. That incident led to protests in the city. The Rijksrecherche is investigating his death as well.

World.title: You can pry Halloween from my cold, witchy fingers
World.content:
You can pry the pumpkins from the cold, dead hands of our regular columnist Molly Quell, who is going to celebrate Halloween despite some Dutch naysayers.

I am throwing a Halloween party. I like Halloween. It has cooler vibes than other second tier holidays (Valentine’s Day, Easter) and less stress than the major ones (Christmas, and for Americans/Canadians, Thanksgiving.)

I have gotten some pushback, however, from some of the Dutchies in my life, who are balking at the “Americanisation” of it all.

“What about Sint Maarten?” a Dutch friend asked me, half joking. The traditional Dutch holiday is celebrated on November 11, named after a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity. Children carry paper lanterns and go house to house, singing, in exchange for sweets.

“You are welcome to celebrate it,” I said. “I don’t.”

“I don’t celebrate Halloween,” she retorted.

“I’ll put you down as a ‘no’ then,” I said.

If my friend does celebrate Sint Maarten, she’s in the minority even in the Netherlands. By some estimates, only 30% of kids are out slinging their lanterns (or in some places, hollowed out turnips) for sweet rewards.

In Utrecht the holiday is celebrated widely, as Sint Maarten is the city’s patron saint. Further afield, however, there’s barely a single flame out on a chilly November evening.

Halloween, on the other hand, is everywhere. Hema has pumpkin candles and Takkie in a witch’s hat. There’s trick-or-treating for kids in community centres, spooky canal tours in Amsterdam, horror movies at every Pathé across the country.

That’s significantly better than a hollowed out turnip.

I admit, the broader point my friend was making is correct. American culture is becoming increasingly dominant and, as many become disillusioned with the United States under the current administration, there will be more and more backlash to things seen as symbols of the country.

There are a lot of American things the Netherlands shouldn’t import. I am on record saying we should ban American influencers from moving here. I am also opposed to importing prudish attitudes towards sex.

Takkie in his little witch’s hat is adorable and I am choosing to defend his (and my) right to celebrate Halloween.

I’ve always been a little surprised that Dutch people don’t embrace Halloween more. They love to dress up in absurd costumes for every other holiday. Have you seen Brabant during Carnival?

Plus, there aren’t really any holidays in autumn. In fact, earlier this year I argued that rather than making Liberation Day (May) a public holiday, as prime minister Rob Jetten suggested, we do Prinsjesdag (September) instead.

Half the country shuts down anyway for the annual announcement of the budget (in 2026, this was even more true, as the train lines were sabotaged) and there’s even a bit of a costume element with the hats.

We need something to celebrate in the fall to take our minds off the impending darkness of winter and Halloween is already right there. It already has built-in rituals, themed food (I will die on this hill defending candy corn) and no obligation to spend time with family.

While the pumpkin spice lattes and the knife-wielding maniacs on film may be an American export, Halloween doesn’t originate in the United States. Historians think it started as a Celtic pagan festival and was taken across the pond by Irish and Scottish immigrants.

And what is a bigger rebuff to the current American administration than celebrating immigration?

World.title: Asylum applications drop 13% under EU migration pact
World.content:
The number of first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands fell by 13% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the same period last year, according to figures from national statistics bureau CBS and immigration service IND.

The downward trend follows the implementation of the new European Union Migration Pact, which came into effect in June this year, with tighter guidelines, the abolition of permanent asylum residence permits and stricter criteria for family reunification.

Several of those changes echo measures pushed by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber (PVV), who promised the “strictest asylum policy ever” and wanted to make the Netherlands “as unattractive as possible to asylum seekers”. Her emergency asylum law was rejected by the Senate in April.

In the third quarter of 2026, some 5,900 people filed an asylum application for the first time, 850 fewer than a year earlier. Asylum applications from Eritreans and Syrians halved, while 1,500 fewer family reunification applicants came to the country than a year ago.

Eritreans submitted the most asylum claims, followed closely by Syrians. According to CBS, the number of Ukrainian applications increased from 15 to 140, while the number of applications from people from Ethiopia decreased from 290 to 75.

World.title: Chaos at Poland’s constitutional court as government-backed judges seek to oust chief justice
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and may be updated as it develops. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) was plunged into chaos on Friday evening as one group of judges, backed by the government, moved to take control of the court from its chief justice, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and President Karol Nawrocki. One of the government-backed judges said that she had suspended the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, from his duties. Police have surrounded the court and were seen preventing Święczkowski from entering the grounds after his supporters had cut through the fence with a power tool. Święczkowski and the opposition claim that an illegal “coup d’etat” is underway. Nawrocki, who had been flying to Senegal for a state visit, ordered his plane to turn around and return to Warsaw. Prezes Świeczkowski wraz z grupą posłów przeciął łańcuchy i próbuje dostać się do trybunału konstytucyjnego. Policja nie chce go przepuścić! Przecież to bezprawie! pic.twitter.com/XbIXigwIi3 — Jan Molski 🇵🇱 (@JanMolski) October 30, 2026 The dramatic events follow a years-long crisis around the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. ‘ That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. Those five judges arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies in parliament and submitted their oaths to the president’s office. However, Święczkowski, who before being appointed as a TK judge had served in the former PiS government, refused to accept those five judges on the court. In doing so, he ignored an order by the European Court of Human Rights that the judges be allowed to take up their positions. Święczkowski argued that the ECHR had no authority to issue such a ruling. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Rumours have long swirled that the government would introduce those judges onto the court by force. PiS supporters have been camped outside the TK grounds for weeks with the aim of preventing that from happening. On Friday evening, large numbers of riot police were deployed around the TK. On the court’s website, a brief statement appeared, saying that a “break in the activities” of Święczkowski and his deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been ordered. The statement did not say who had ordered that break, but it cited article 130 of the law on common courts, under which the president of a court or the justice minister can order an immediate break in a judge’s official duties if they are caught in the act of committing an offence. However, Marcin Matczak, a prominent scholar of constitutional law who was also a critic of PiS’ judicial reforms, wrote on social media, that, while the justice minister exercises oversight over common courts, he cannot do so over the TK. “I consider Bogdan Święczkowski to be the worst person to serve as the president of the TK,” wrote Matczak. “I never thought I’d end up defending him, but this legal basis [for suspending Święczkowski] is nonexistent for a million reasons.” Ze szczątkowych informacji, na jakiej podstawie zawieszono B. Święczkowskiego, wynika, że ma to być art. 19 ustawy o statusie sędziów TK, który mówi, że do spraw nieuregulowanych w tej ustawie stosuje się „przepisy dotyczące praw i obowiązków sędziów SN” i art. 130 ustawy o SN,… — Marcin Matczak (@wsamraz) October 30, 2026 Meanwhile, Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, issued a statement announcing that he had submitted motions to the TK to waive the immunity from prosecution of Świeczkowski and Sochański. He said that the documents had been “delivered to the longest-serving judge of the Constitutional Tribunal”. That was a reference to Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the TK judges whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. She told state broadcaster TVP that it was she who had issued the order to suspend Święczkowski from his duties. She justified her action by accusing Święczkowski of blocking judges from taking up their positions and of overseeing irregularities in the assignment of judges to cases, reports Polskie Radio. Korwin-Piotrowska’s claim to have the longest tenure among TK judges relates not to her service on tribunal itself, but to the fact that she first began her judicial career in 1995. 🗣️ “Bogdan Święczkowski narusza zasady funkcjonowania TK. (…) Nie było innego wyjścia” – sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska w TVP Info. pic.twitter.com/22FYJJbQAC — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 30, 2026 While the TK website appears to now be under the control of Korwin-Piotrowska, the court’s account on social media service X issued a statement saying that “an unlawful takeover of the TK’s website has occurred”, that “Bogdan Święczkowski remains chief justice”, and that “Korwin-Piotrowska is not a TK judge”. “All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d’état,” it added. Nastąpiło bezprawne przejęcie strony internetowej Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Prezesem @TK_GOV_PL jest nadal Bogdan Święczkowski, a Wiceprezesem Bartłomiej Sochański. Pani Anna Korwin-Piotrowska nie jest sędzią Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Wszystkie osoby uczestniczące w… — Trybunał Konstytucyjny (@TK_GOV_PL) October 30, 2026 The court’s spokeswoman, Weronika Ścibor, told broadcaster Kanał Zero that “seven people elected as [TK] judges this year” had been escorted into the building by officers from the State Protection Service (SOP), a body responsible for protecting state officials. SOP is subordinate to the interior minister. She said they had entered the grounds of the court through a gate that leads from the prime minister’s chancellery, rather than the main entrance from the street where protesters are gathered. Korwin-Piotrowska also confirmed to TVP that she was one of seven judges who were inside the TK on Friday evening. Rzeczniczka Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Weronika Ścibor komentuje sytuację w TK. Według jej relacji siedem osób wybranych na sędziów weszło do budynku w asyście funkcjonariuszy SOP, natomiast wiceprezes Bartłomiej Sochański nie został wpuszczony na teren Trybunału. pic.twitter.com/VwxU4UrYuz — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) October 30, 2026 The developments at the court prompted outrage from the opposition. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński declared outside the court that “as of today, Poland has become a police state, and from there it’s a straight path to authoritarianism, and then to totalitarianism”. Kaczyński called on Nawrocki to return to Poland from his state visit to Senegal and defend the court. The president himself quickly confirmed that he had done so, with flight trackers showing his plane turning around in midair and heading back to Poland. Meanwhile, Zbigniew Kapiński, the chief justice of the Supreme Court – a separate entity from the Constitutional Tribunal – told Kanał Zero that he was “appalled” by what was happening, which was “undoubtedly a coup d’etat”. Our most tracked flight right now: A Polish government aircraft en route to Senegal is now returning to Warsaw. https://t.co/YdLhQmV8pl pic.twitter.com/Dz9KPgI3eI — Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) October 30, 2026 Tusk, however, issued a statement on social media defending what was taking place at the TK. “Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” he wrote. “After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland approves first fast-track renewable energy zones
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced its first fast-track zones for renewable energy projects as the coal-dependent country seeks to speed up its transition to cleaner sources of electricity. The regional assembly in Wielkopolska province, western Poland, this week approved plans covering 105.4 hectares across four municipalities, where investors will be able to develop solar farms under simplified planning and environmental procedures. The environment ministry estimates that the changes, introduced under an EU directive, could reduce project preparation times from three to four years down to just one or two years. Pierwsze #OPRO już są! Sejmik województwa wielkopolskiego przyjął dziś pierwsze w Polsce plany OPRO. Obejmą one ok. 105,4 ha w gminach Lwówek, Rawicz, Słupca i Złotów.🔆 ❓Czym jest OPRO? ✅To Obszary Przyspieszonego Rozwoju #OZE, czyli tereny, na których – już podczas ich… — Marek Pogorzelski (@rzeczni_MKiS) October 26, 2026 Under the scheme, planning and much of the environmental assessment will be completed before investors apply for permits, allowing projects to move forward more quickly. Environmental authorities will also have a maximum of 45 days to review projects with a capacity of at least 150 kW. Industry representatives told energy Świat OZE, a renewable energy news service, that obtaining an environmental decision can currently take up to 150 days. The newly designated areas, known as Accelerated Renewable Energy Development Zones (OPRO), will be located in the municipalities of Złotów, Lwówek, Rawicz and Słupca. Together, they have an estimated technical potential of 66-80 megawatts of solar capacity, depending on the arrangement of the panels. Maria Niewitała-Rej, a climate and energy policy analyst at the Reform Institute, a Warsaw-based think tank, told the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna newspaper that while “the scale of the Wielkopolska plan is modest, the adoption of the first resolutions is a step in the right direction”. The creation of accelerated renewable energy development zones stems from the EU’s revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), which requires member states to designate areas where renewable energy projects can be developed more quickly. Under the directive, permitting procedures in these zones should take no longer than 12 months for onshore projects and 24 months for offshore projects. EU rules required the first zones to be designated by 21 February 2026, making Poland’s adoption several months late. Polish state mining firm JSW, which is the EU's largest producer of coking coal and one of Poland's biggest employers, has announced that it will cut over 4,000 jobs, 21% of its workforce, by the end of this year as it seeks to stem large financial losses https://t.co/EWP3rAVMaH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Poland has long had one of Europe’s most polluting energy sectors. The country still produces around half of its electricity from coal, by far the higher proportion in the EU. However, the share of renewables has grown significantly in recent years. It nearly doubled from 14.7% of the energy mix in 2021 to 29.4% in 2025. Onshore wind was the largest contributor last year, accounting for 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. Poland’s national energy and climate plan, approved in June, envisages coal accounting for just 0-5% of the energy mix by 2040. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%). Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish Left seeks to end state funding of clergy’s social contributions as government reform stalls
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Left, a junior partner in Poland’s ruling coalition, has proposed a bill to abolish the Church Fund, which provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy. It says it is frustrated by delays in fulfilling a pledge made by most parties in the wide ruling coalition to reform the fund. However, another coalition partner, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), says that it will oppose the bill, calling instead for a system allowing taxpayers to allocate part of their taxes to religious institutions of their choice. Senior church figures also say they have not been consulted. 📣 Lewica składa ustawę likwidującą Fundusz Kościelny. Czas na realizację umowy koalicyjnej w zakresie świeckiego państwa‼️ Co zakłada nasz projekt? ⬇️ ✅ Składki na duchownych przestają być w 80 procentach finansowane z budżetu państwa jak dotychczas. 50% składek pokrywać… pic.twitter.com/syqUMdCugr — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 29, 2026 The Church Fund, originally established in 1950 to compensate religious communities for property seized by the communist authorities, provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy, for religious organisations’ charitable activities, and for the renovation of religious buildings. It now supports all legally recognised religious denominations in Poland, including those that did not lose property at the time. Last year, the state spent 275.7 million zloty on the Church Fund. This year it has budgeted 272.6 million zloty. Most of this money is then used to cover 80% of clergy members’ social security contributions. Under the bill proposed by The Left, churches would pay half of the contributions, with clergy covering the other half. For regular workers, such contributions are funded jointly by employees and their employers, Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus, pointed out, as quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We are introducing the same arrangement for priests and members of the clergy.” At least 17.5bn zloty in state funds went to religious bodies from 2021-23, with over 95% going to Catholic organisations, the state auditor has found. In response, the speaker of parliament has proposed measures to reduce and better oversee such spending https://t.co/IN3dpY4La2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 16, 2025 An exception is made in the bill for members of enclosed religious orders and missionaries, who would have their contributions paid in full by their churches. The cost of maintaining historic churches would be covered by the National Fund for the Protection of Monuments, Żukowska explained. Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is the leader of The Left as well as the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful chamber in the Polish parliament, said the party did not oppose religion but wanted clergy to be treated equally under the law. “I would like to remind my coalition partners: our coalition agreement includes a commitment to work toward establishing the principles of a secular state in Poland,” he said, speaking alongside Żukowska. “Our patience is running out”. Ahead of the 2023 election, both the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and The Left pledged to abolish the Church Fund, while the centre-right Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) proposed replacing state funding with voluntary taxpayer contributions. PSL had no equivalent formal party-wide pledge. In 2024, after the coalition came to power, Tusk announced plans to reform the fund and appointed a government working group led by the PSL leader and deputy prime minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. The group’s work has since stalled. Kosiniak-Kamysz yesterday dismissed The Left’s proposal, saying it has “not the slightest chance of support in parliament”. His party, the second largest in the coalition with 32 of 239 MPs, sees the existing fund as an inexpensive form of compensation and will oppose abolishing it, he vowed. Instead, taxpayers should be able to allocate part of their taxes to a religious institution of their choice, a system used in several European countries, to “let the Polish people themselves decide whether or not they want to contribute,” he said, quoted by broadcaster Polsat News. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński, a member of Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO), said that he supported reform, but criticised The Left for submitting the bill without consulting its coalition partners. A long-term decline in trust in the Catholic church in Poland has accelerated over the last year, with only 35% of Poles now saying they trust the church. Meanwhile, the armed forces now enjoy record-high trust of 94% https://t.co/ErCBE4HwWR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 17, 2025 Religious communities also criticised the proposal for not having been discussed with them in advance. In a press statement sent to PAP, the Polish Episcopal Conference (KEP), the main organ of the Catholic church in Poland, said any solution should comply with the country’s agreement with the Vatican, as well as the constitutional principle that relations between the state and religious communities be regulated by mutual agreement. Bishop Jerzy Samiec, head of the Evangelical-Augsburg Church in Poland, the country’s biggest Protestant body, pointed to the significant costs churches face in maintaining their properties, including care homes and other facilities. The Catholic Church, Poland’s dominant religious institution, has seen a long-term decline in public trust, with only 35% of Poles saying they trusted it in 2025. That has coincided with a series of crises in recent years, in particular over revelations of child sexual abuse by members of the clergy and negligence in dealing with them by the church hierarchy. A variety of surveys, including from the church itself, show that religious attendance and identification have been declining in Poland in recent years. A growing number of Poles are turning away from the Catholic church, but not from religious belief itself. This creates challenges for the church, but also for Polish identity, which has historically been linked to Catholicism, writes Katarzyna Skiba https://t.co/udWGzd0X7F — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 18, 2023 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU. However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a “consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state” with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a “parody”. But soon, said Kaczyński, “a window of opportunity” for reform may appear because “completely different governments could emerge” in Poland, France and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year. PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day. He warned that the incoming opposition government will "strive to implement this plan" and called on Poles to "fight" against it https://t.co/QDbxmiaazJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2023 Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties. However, the PiS leader then warned that, “if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force”. Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties “include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU. This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations”. “It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,” he added. The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before. “Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,” wrote Tusk himself on X. “This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.” “So they do want Polexit after all,” wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania…An end to subsidies for farmers and investments…And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.” In a video published later on Thursday, Tusk declared that next year’s parliamentary elections would help decide “whether Poland remains in the European Union or leaves it”. Jarosław Kaczyński ogłosił właśnie, że Polska powinna zacząć rokowania o warunkach wyjścia z Unii Europejskiej. O taką między innymi stawkę toczy się dziś w Polsce walka. Twarda walka. Nie zamierzam jej przegrać, nawet jeśli nie wszyscy zagrają ze mną. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 29, 2026 Kaczyński responded by saying that “Tusk is lying as usual”. He emphasised that he believes “the EU is needed but it requires thorough reform” so that it “benefits not the elites, but ordinary citizens”. PiS deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek said on Thursday that his party was “considering all scenarios, including the possibility that the EU will kill itself”. However, he added that the priority remained reforming the bloc and “PiS has no plans to leave the EU”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). When PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it regularly clashed with Brussels over a variety of issues, including judicial reform, trade, climate policy, and migration. Since Tusk, a former president of the European Council, took power in 2023, his government has greatly improved relations with Brussels. Tusk jak zwykle kłamie. Najwyraźniej wychodzi z założenia, że dzień bez kłamstwa jest dniem straconym… Unia Europejska jest potrzebna, ale wymaga gruntownej reformy. Kryzys i zapaść w jej obecnym kształcie to efekt rządów Merkel i jednego z jej pomocników, Tuska. Nie ma co się… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) October 29, 2026 Poland has been the largest net recipient of EU funding since joining the bloc in 2004. A study published earlier this year found that the country’s economy is 42% larger than it would have been had Poland not been part of the EU. Opinion polls consistently show a large majority of Poles in favour of remaining part of the EU. However, recent years have seen an uptick in support for Polexit, as well as for anti-EU far-right parties. PiS has increasingly found itself competing against such parties for votes. Regular polling by state research agency CBOS shows that, while opposition to EU membership fell to a record low of 5% in 2022, it has subsequently risen and stood at 14% in the most recent survey. World.title: Polish bishop convicted for failing to promptly report child sex abuse allegations
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the first ruling of its kind in Poland, a Catholic bishop has been found guilty of failing to promptly inform the law enforcement authorities about allegations of child sex abuse committed by priests under his authority. Andrzej Jeż, the bishop of Tarnów, was handed a non-custodial sentence that will require him to donate 25% of his earnings for two years to a charity that supports victims of child sexual abuse. However, the verdict can still be appealed, and the diocese of Tarnów has already announced that it “disagrees with the court’s ruling” and that an appeal will be filed. Pierwszy taki wyrok w Polsce. Biskup skazany za zwlekanie z powiadomieniem prokuratury o pedofilach w sutannach Ordynariusz tarnowski bp Andrzej Jeż jest pierwszym biskupem oskarżonym o zbyt późne powiadomienie prokuratury o pedofilii w Kościele. I pierwszym, który który został… — Bartosz T. Wieliński 🇵🇱🇪🇺🇺🇦🇬🇱 (@Bart_Wielinski) October 29, 2026 The case relates to alleged abuse by two priests who worked under Jeż’s authority. They can be identified only as Stanisław P. and Tomasz K. under Polish privacy law. In 2022, prosecutors discontinued an investigation into allegations against Stanisław P. because the statute of limitations had expired, despite concluding that he had harmed at least 95 children and committed “sexual acts” against 77 of them over several decades in parishes in Poland and Ukraine. In 2023, prosecutors decided to charge Tomasz K., who allegedly sexually abused children as early as 2018. However, they have been unable to formally present the charges to him because of his poor health, news website OKO.press reported earlier this year. Though Jeż was not accused of complicity in the alleged abuse itself, he was charged under a 2017 law making it a criminal offence not to “immediately notify the authorities” of “credible information” about sexual abuse of minors. The offence is punishable by up to three years in prison. Investigators say that, although an internal church probe into Stanisław P. was initiated in the 2000s and a decision to remove him from the clergy was made in 2013, Jeż only notified the prosecutor’s office in 2020. In the case of Tomasz K., the bishop notified prosecutors only in 2021. In court, prosecutor Marcin Stępień said that Jeż’s failure to report the abuse promptly had allowed the statute of limitations to expire in the case of some of Stanisław P.’s victims. Stępień also noted that the bishop had only come forward with the information when media coverage brought the allegations against Stanisław P. to light, reports broadcaster TVN. A church commission set up to investigate child sex abuse in a Catholic diocese in Poland has identified at least 50 victims and 29 abusers. It also found that bishops repeatedly failed to take action when credible reports of abuse were submitted to them https://t.co/MRNl5vWp4E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 13, 2026 Prosecutors sought a 10-month prison sentence, suspended for three years, and a fine of 20,000 zloty (€4,550). Jeż, however, denied the allegations against him and sought an acquittal. He argued that he had reported the alleged abuse to the authorities as soon as there was credible information. On Thursday, the court found the bishop guilty, giving him a sentence known as “restriction of liberty” (ograniczenie wolnośći), under which a convict is not imprisoned but required to do some kind of social good. In Jeż’s case, the court ordered that 25% of his salary for two years be donated to the Empowering Children Foundation (Dajemy Dzieciom Siłę), which supports victims of child abuse. He was additionally ordered to pay 20,000 zloty to the Fund for Assistance to Victims and Post-Penitentiary Assistance. In a statement after the verdict was issued, the diocese of Tarnów said that it “disagreed with the court’s ruling” and that, after a written justification from the court was reviewed, “an appeal will be filed”. The Catholic church in Poland has in recent years been hit by a series of revelations regarding historical abuse of minors by members of the clergy and allegations that bishops covered cases up. The Vatican has taken action against a number of Polish bishops over the issue. Most recently, in 2024, the Vatican announced the resignation of the bishop of Łowicz, Andrzej Dziuba, due to his “negligence in handling cases of sexual abuse against minors”. In February, a commission created by the diocese of Sosnowiec following a series of scandals announced that it had identified at least 50 children who were harmed and 29 people suspected of abusing minors, most of them members of the clergy. World.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Turkish software engineer has, with the help of AI and vast quantities of Polish public data, created a precise digital replica of Warsaw, the city where he lives. The map, which can be explored for free online, features almost 200,000 buildings, moving trams that match their real-life schedules, changing light and weather conditions, and over 45,000 accurately placed streetlamps that turn on at night. It is even possible to fly a virtual plane through the city. The person behind the project, Bedirhan Yildirim, was inspired by recent efforts to produce similar maps of New York and London. While he initially considered producing one of Istanbul, his hometown, he decided instead to pick the city he lives in, Warsaw. “It is smaller, mostly flat, and I walk its streets every day,” he explained of his choice. Yildirim then used AI coding agents to create the map through a process of trial and error, constantly tweaking and improving the model. The initial version took only two days to produce and was launched on 22 October, but it has been regularly improved since then based on feedback from users. The work was made possible by what Yildirim says is the “incredible amount of data” Poland’s national mapping office, GUGiK, provides for free, including 3D building models, terrain scans, and even details of almost 2 million trees. Further information, including on parks, streetlamps, and traffic lights, was taken from OpenStreetMap, a freely licensed database. Meanwhile, timetables from Warsaw’s public transport authority, ZTM, and Poland’s national rail operator, PKP, allowed the map to feature accurately timed trams and trains. Current weather conditions are input from Open-Meteo, an open-source meteorological service. But users can also choose to manually adjust the time of day or year, with light and weather changing accordingly. An observation deck at the top of the EU's tallest building, Varso Tower in Warsaw, has opened to the public. Located 230m up on the tower's 53rd floor, the attraction offers a 360° panorama of Poland's capital.https://t.co/VeEapOmh4s — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 9, 2025 The result is an incredible level of explorable detail, from major landmarks, such as the communist-era Palace of Culture and Science and Varso Tower, the EU’s tallest building, down to the seating steps and bars along the Vistula River boulevards. The map also features graveyards reflecting Warsaw and Poland’s diverse past, including Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Jewish and Tatar Muslim graves. Around 1 November, when Poles visit cemeteries around All Saints’ Day, candles glow around the graves. A final touch Yildirim has added is a flight simulator, allowing users to travel over the city – and complete missions – in a Cessna aeroplane, an air ambulance, a flying car, or even a UFO that takes off from the Copernicus Science Centre and travels to the National Stadium. I turned Warsaw into a flight sim 🛩️ Take off from Chopin, fly through the ring over the Palace of Culture, then land a UFO inside Stadion Narodowy as the roof opens 🛸 Desktop only for now. Can you land it? 👇 pic.twitter.com/DT2fdk1Vem — Bedirhan (@bedcodes) October 27, 2026 Speaking to Notes from Poland, Yildirim says that he moved to Poland in 2022 to pursue a job in IT before starting his own business. Initially living in Kraków, the country’s second-largest city, he then moved to Warsaw in 2025. Asked what his own personal favourite places in the city are, Yildirim points to Warsaw’s parks, such as Skaryszewski, Pole Mokotowskie and Łazienki. His favourite neighbourhood is Saska Kępa on the right bank of the Vistula. The software engineer adds that his project is an example of how AI can be an “amazing tool to do 90% of the job very quickly”. The remaining 10% of human input “is what keeps it from being ‘AI slop'”. Yildirim says that, without the use of AI, the map of Warsaw he created would have needed an entire team to build over a period of months. World.title: Poland detains Ukrainian accused of arson attack in Romania on behalf of Russia
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained a Ukrainian citizen who is wanted by Romania on suspicion of involvement in an arson attack on a defence company carried out on behalf of Russia. On Tuesday, the Polish police’s Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) announced that anti-terrorism officers had detained the man, who can be named only as Artem S. under Polish privacy law, in Warsaw under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Romania. In the early hours of 14 September, a fire broke out in the city of Brașov, Romania, in the immediate vicinity of premises belonging to Carfil, a manufacturer of military equipment. Carfil is a subsidiary of ROMARM, a state-owned defence company. On Monday this week, the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) said it had determined that the fire had been deliberately caused by a “sabotage network coordinated from Russia”. It added that “several citizens of former Soviet states who reside in the EU” had been involved in the arson attack. The SRI also revealed that the group’s activities were not limited to Romania. “Its coordinators in Russia had assigned it a wide range of targets across the region, including state-owned and private arms manufacturing facilities, as well as sites of military and industrial interest.” In a separate statement, Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organised Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) confirmed that the suspects were a Ukrainian, who was at large in Poland, and two Belarusians, who had already been detained in Germany, where they “had been preparing to commit similar acts”. Polish broadcaster RMF reports, based on sources, that Artem S.’s role in the Brașov attack was to identify a target and to arrange payment for those involved. A Polish court will now decide whether the 25-year-old should be extradited to Romania. Poland itself has been a primary target for Russia’s campaign of sabotage and other so-called “hybrid actions” in Europe. Many of those detained and convicted have been Ukrainian and Belarusians, though some Polish citizens have also been implicated. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 In some cases, such operatives are amateurs – so-called “disposable agents” – recruited, coordinated and paid through messaging service Telegram. Some have also been pre-existing criminal groups hired by Russia to carry out such tasks. In August, a drone production plant belonging to private Polish arms company WB Electronics was targeted in an arson attack that Poland has blamed on Russia. The following month, a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was likewise hit by an arson attack that Poland blamed on Russia. Two Turkish men were later detained in Germany on suspicion of carrying out the attack. World.title: Poland and UK sign Warsaw Defence Plan to “deter Russian threats”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland and the United Kingdom have signed the Warsaw Defence Plan, an agreement to enhance their cooperation on security. The aim, says the British Ministry of Defence, is to “deter Russian threats”. The plan, which follows on from the two countries signing a strategic defence partnership earlier this year, will include joint development and production of defence technologies and military exercises in the Baltic Sea. The UK and Poland share a deep and historical defence partnership. Today, Defence Secretary @WesStreeting signed the Warsaw Defence Plan to bring our two nations’ Armed Forces and industries closer together and help ensure collective security in Europe. 🇬🇧🤝🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/IP98D1Qs1L — Ministry of Defence 🇬🇧 (@DefenceHQ) October 27, 2026 “Poland is one of the UK’s closest allies – from flying together in the Battle of Britain, to breaking the Enigma code, they have been a vital partner for our defence for nearly a century,” said British defence secretary Wes Streeting on a visit to Warsaw. “The new Warsaw Defence Plan honours this cooperation and sets out how we will continue to work together today, building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO,” he added. His Polish counterpart, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, declared that “the Polish-British alliance has never been as strong as it is now”. Both he and Streeting also emphasised the importance of working together to support Ukraine. Among the aims listed for the plan are collaboration in the development and manufacture of next-generation air-defence missiles, as well as drones and counter-drone technologies. Earlier this year, Poland and the UK, along with Germany, France and Italy, agreed to jointly develop and procure air-defence systems, including missiles and drones. The Warsaw Defence Plan also pledges to “increase defensive maritime activity in the Baltic Sea through exercises and regional coordination, helping British and Polish forces protect vital lines of communication in the sea”. The two countries will also seek to build upon existing cooperation between their defence industries, including Poland’s purchase of CAMM-ER surface-to-air missiles and 100 launchers from MBDA and last year’s strategic partnership on ammunition production between Poland’s PGZ and Britain’s BAE Systems. Poland and the UK have signed a major new defence and security treaty. The agreement includes plans to jointly develop a new air-defence missile, hold large-scale military exercises, and cooperate on countering Russian hybrid attacks https://t.co/cXeYT2u1lw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 27, 2026 This week’s agreement builds upon the Northolt Treaty signed by Poland and the UK in May this year, under which the two countries agreed to cooperate more closely on security. Last year, Poland signed a similar agreement upgrading relations with France. That followed a strategic partnership agreement with Sweden the previous year. In April this year, Poland signed new comprehensive strategic partnership agreements with South Korea and Japan. This year, it has also deepened security ties with Canada and Norway. In November, Poland will host the first military exercises organised by the so-called Coalition of the Willing. Thousands of personnel from the UK, Poland, France and Germany will test operational readiness for a multinational force to secure a potential future Ukraine peace deal. World.title: Prague to Begin Winter Maintenance of Roads and Sidewalks on November 1
World.content:
Prague will begin its annual winter road maintenance programme on November 1.

Until the end of March, the Technical Administration of Communications (TSK) will be responsible for keeping roads, sidewalks and other public routes accessible to vehicles and pedestrians.

Maintenance priorities are determined by the importance of individual routes for traffic and local residents. Roads and pedestrian areas are divided into several categories, each with specific deadlines for snow and ice clearance.



Residents can check the designated maintenance routes and the type of work planned for each area through the city’s online Winter Maintenance application (Zimní údržba).

Road maintenance is divided into three priority categories. The first covers 1,399 kilometres of the city’s busiest roads, which must be treated within two to four hours of maintenance crews being deployed.

The second category includes 519 kilometres of roads, with a clearance deadline of 12 hours. The third covers another 346 kilometres, where maintenance must be completed within 48 hours after the first- and second-priority routes have been treated.

Sidewalks, cycle paths and other pedestrian routes follow a separate schedule. The first category includes 1,063 kilometres, which must be serviced within 12 hours. The second covers a further 693 kilometres, with work required by 5 p.m. on the day after maintenance of the first category has been completed.

Altogether, Prague’s winter maintenance programme covers 2,264 kilometres of roads and 1,756 kilometres of sidewalks and other pedestrian routes.

From December 1 to March 31, temporary workers will help clear sidewalks in parts of Prague 6 that are more difficult to reach with standard maintenance equipment.

These include Hanspaulka, Baba, Sedlec, the Šárecké Valley and parts of Ořechovka.

World.title: Prague Appears in Apple’s Latest MacBook Pro Commercial
World.content:
Prague has once again provided the backdrop for an Apple advertising campaign.

The American technology company has released a new commercial promoting its latest MacBook Pro, featuring several recognisable locations across the Czech capital.

The two-minute video centres on the Prague Congress Centre, with additional scenes filmed around Vyšehrad and Karlovo náměstí. Although Apple does not identify the locations in the commercial, viewers familiar with Prague will recognise several of the city’s landmarks.



The Congress Centre plays the largest role in the production. Its glass-walled entrance hall, with views of the Nusle Bridge, features in several sequences.

The commercial also shows people working on laptops at long rows of tables on an upper floor, alongside an overhead view of the building’s spiral staircase and its metal sculpture The Sun, created by Czech artist Vladimír Procházka.

The production also moved outdoors, using the historic fortifications of Vyšehrad as a setting. Another location is the park at Karlovo náměstí, where the monument to Czech physician and naturalist Jan Evangelista Purkyně can be seen.

Not all the Prague scenery in the  is entirely authentic. In some sequences, Apple has used computer-generated imagery to modify the views through the Congress Centre’s windows, replacing the familiar city panorama with skyscrapers and mountain landscapes.

The latest production continues Apple’s history of filming s in the Czech Republic.

Two years ago, the company also used Prague locations for an iPhone 16 Pro campaign, which featured the roof of the Prague Congress Centre and the Vyšehrad area, alongside the sandstone formations of the Prachov Rocks in the Bohemian Paradise region.

The new MacBook Pro introduces a touchscreen for the first time in Apple’s laptop range. The device is powered by the company’s M5 Pro and M5 Max processors. In the Czech Republic, prices start at CZK 84,990, with sales scheduled to begin on November 6.

World.title: Guitar Legend Carlos Santana to Return to Czech Republic in 2027
World.content:
Legendary guitarist Carlos Santana will return to the Czech Republic on July 22, 2027, for an outdoor concert in the Castle Gardens of Slavkov u Brna, near Brno.

The ten-time Grammy Award winner will perform as part of his Planet of Free Will Global Tour 2027, bringing more than five decades of music to the Czech audience.

Known for blending rock, blues, jazz and Latin rhythms, Santana has built a distinctive sound that has influenced generations of musicians and listeners.



His performance at the 1969 Woodstock festival helped establish him as an international star, while early albums such as Santana*(1969) and Abraxas (1970) produced classics including “Evil Ways,” “Black Magic Woman” and “Oye Como Va.”

Santana reached another career milestone with the 1999 album Supernatural, which featured collaborations with artists including Rob Thomas. The record became a global hit, spawning the singles “Smooth” and “Maria Maria” and winning nine Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year.

Over his career, Santana has received ten Grammy Awards and three Latin Grammy Awards. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998, received the Kennedy Center Honors and was ranked 11th on *Rolling Stone* magazine’s list of the 100 greatest guitarists of all time.

Despite his long career, Santana continues to release new music and perform internationally. His live shows are known for extended guitar solos, Latin-inspired rhythms and a mix of classic hits and newer material.

Tickets will cost CZK 2,000, plus booking fees.

General ticket sales start on October 30, 2026, at noon, through Ticketmaster and Ticketportal.

World.title: Prague Metronome Lets People Donate to Charity for Just 50 CZK
World.content:
Prague’s Metronome is taking on a charitable role through a new initiative that allows people to pay for a minute of illumination while supporting one of six nonprofit organizations.

The project, called Puls města (City Pulse), was launched by real estate company PSN, which operates the landmark on Letná Hill. Donations start at 50 Czech crowns, and participants can choose which organization they want to support.



The new initiative connects its lighting system with fundraising, allowing members of the public to contribute through the project’s website.

Six Colors, Six Charitable Causes

Each participating organization is represented by a different color. Red supports the Tereza Maxová Foundation for Children, while light blue represents the Kapka naděje (Drop of Hope) Endowment Fund.

Yellow is associated with Díky, že můžem, an initiative focused on civic engagement and democratic values. Pink represents Pink Crocodile, dark blue supports the AutTalk Endowment Fund, founded by Kateřina Sokolová, and green is dedicated to the Fund for Endangered Children.

Visitors can select a cause and make a contribution directly through the project’s website.

Donations Start at 50 CZK

Contributions range from 50 to 9,999 CZK. Regardless of the amount donated, each payment purchases exactly one minute of illumination. A larger contribution therefore does not extend the lighting time.

The website also displays the amount raised for each organization, allowing donors to follow the campaign’s progress. A virtual queue shows when each participant’s turn is scheduled, with the expected time provided after payment.

World.title: Prague’s Golden Eye to Host Japanese Brunch With Live Chef Demonstrations
World.content:
Prague’s Golden Eye bar at Fairmont Hotel is hosting a Japanese-inspired brunch combining traditional ceremonies, live sushi preparation, premium food and signature cocktails.

The afternoon will begin with Kagami Biraki, a traditional Japanese sake barrel-opening ceremony often associated with celebrations and new beginnings.



Guests will then be able to watch a live tuna carving, one of the event’s main attractions.

The programme will also include omakase bites, with chefs preparing sushi at a live station. Guests can pair the food with signature cocktails and a curated selection of wines throughout the afternoon.

A live DJ will provide the soundtrack, adding music to the Japanese-inspired dining experience.

The event is designed exclusively for adults, with tickets priced at CZK 7,900 per person. Full prepayment is required to secure a booking.

Reservations can be made through Golden Eye’s online booking page.

World.title: Hip-Hop Star Xzibit Coming to Prague’s Roxy on November 17
World.content:
West Coast rap legend Xzibit will perform at Prague’s ROXY on November 17, bringing his show featuring tracks from his latest album and some of his best-known hits.

Presented by Gotobeat and Enjoy Events, the show will feature music from *Kingmaker*, alongside career highlights including “X,” “Multiply,” “Paparazzi” and “What’s the Difference.”



Xzibit returns with new album Kingmaker

A major name in West Coast hip-hop since the 1990s, Xzibit built his reputation through his distinctive deep voice, forceful delivery and collaborations with some of the genre’s biggest artists.

His albums Restless, Man vs. Machine and Weapons of Mass Destruction helped establish him as one of the defining rappers of his generation. His work with Dr. Dre, Eminem, Snoop Dogg and Ice Cube further cemented his place in hip-hop, while his television career brought him to a wider audience as the host of MTV’s Pimp My Ride.

Released on May 16, 2025, Kingmaker marked Xzibit’s first solo studio album since 2012.

The 20-track record brings together established names and newer voices, with guest appearances from Dr. Dre, Ice Cube, Busta Rhymes, Ty Dolla $ign, Royce da 5’9”, Redman and B-Real.

The album combines the sound that made Xzibit famous with a more contemporary production style, reflecting on his decades in the music industry while introducing his work to a new generation of listeners.
